Not two weeks later, the town's police department found not only were the cameras still on, but they continued to record vehicles, using infrared technology for the dark trash-bag induced conditions.

Excelsior Springs Police Department took to Facebook on November 5 to inform its residents of the issue. The department's Lieutenant Ryan Dowdy told Local 12 that the city initially placed bags over the cameras when they voted to end its contract with Flock and remove the cameras. However, not only are the cameras still on, the black garbage bags do not seem to block Flock's automated license plate reader's infrared technology. The company touts that tech on its own website as "nighttime performance that doesn't quit."
Also problematic is that with a cancelled contract the police department cannot access or use the data but other law enforcement agencies might be able to.

The 15 cameras installed in the town have recorded some vehicles, Dowdy said that most of these images have been headlights and taillights, with a few license plates. The screenshot image shared to Excelsior Springs Police Department's Facebook page showed a few of the vehicles captured through the garbage bags with the infrared. The third of the semi-hazy images showed a red box over the license plate it captured.

About a month ago, the police department held an informative session with the people of Excelsior Springs to explain Flock's ALPR technology to citizens. Community concerns still prevailed in taking down the cameras, as the council voted unanimously a couple of weeks later to cancel the contract. Although the police department said not using the 15 cameras posted in town will affect its police work, Dowdy said it continues efforts to be honest with area residents.
"You know, we'd rather tell people, be upfront about it," Dowdy said. "We're not trying to hide anything. To be honest, we haven't looked at it until yesterday to even find that it was occurring."

The city's solution for now is to double-bag the cameras until they are removed, hopefully some time around the contract's end at the end of this month. This latest folly is another warning to towns, cities and communities that have gone about covering their cameras with trash bags to double up. Who knows what kind of trash can seep through just the one layer.

title: Disney Testing AI-Powered 'Cars'-Themed Parking Assistants
raw_summary: Your next trip to Disneyland may look a little different. The Walt Disney Company has revealed it is testing AI-powered robot assistants that will help drivers find a parking space at the company's crowded resorts. Finding a convenient parking space at a Disneyland resort can be stressful for even the most patient drivers, so these robots could be a godsend. How Disney plans to protect them from rogue drivers remains to be seen. These robots — inspired by "Cars" and "Wall-E" characters — were previewed during the recent Disney Accelerator Demo Day. They are being tested in partnership with Field AI, a robotics firm founded in 2023 with former staff from Google's DeepMind, NASA, Nvidia, Tesla, and others. While a lot of focus in the robotics field is on advanced humanoid robots similar to those from Tesla, Boston Dynamics, and several Chinese firms, these parking assistants haven't been designed to look like a person.

They are being tested in partnership with Field AI, a robotics firm founded in 2023 with former staff from Google's DeepMind, NASA, Nvidia, Tesla, and others. While a lot of focus in the robotics field is on advanced humanoid robots similar to those from Tesla, Boston Dynamics, and several Chinese firms, these parking assistants haven't been designed to look like a person.

Instead, one of the small robots previewed is a tiny four-wheeler not dissimilar to some of the self-driving food delivery robots used in the U.S. One of these robots was shown painted bright orange and with bright yellow accents to mimic a fluorescent vest. It then includes a large screen in place of a traditional windshield, complete with eyes that move and active eyelids, just like the beloved characters from "Cars."

Positioned atop of the autonomous robot's roof is a changing sign that points drivers in the direction of a parking space. Additionally, the robot includes two small arms with red lights to also guide drivers, much like an aircraft marshaller. The robots look very cute, but we suspect they're also very expensive. With stressed parents trying to park and excitable kids in the backseat, we suspect more than a few of these parking assistant robots could be hit, either accidentally or intentionally.

Disney hasn't provided any timeline as to when these robotic parking assistants could be deployed, nor has it guaranteed that they will indeed be deployed at Disneyland locations. While they may be less prone to errors than human parking assistants, the initial outlay on them won't come cheap. We'd hate to think how much the cost of these robots will add to the prices of Disney's already-ballooning admission rates — the average cost for a family of four to get into the park costs between $476 and $836.

raw_summary: Ever since Skipp Sudduth asked for “Something very Fast. Audi S8. Something that can shove a little bit,” in 1998's Ronin , Audi's big body sedan has been the stuff of legend. Mercedes-Benz S-Class ? Too obvious. BMW 7-Series ? You don't want to look like a wannabe James Bond. But an Audi A8? That's what you drive when you have a nickname like The Transporter . Thus, Audi has just pressed pause on production of the A8, with no immediate plans in place to reboot it.

The Neckarsulm plant where the A8 was being built has already pivoted to production of the Audi A5 in both sedan and Avant forms, in standard and S5 or RS5 trims. Audi has been headquartered in Ingolstadt since the 1980s, long enough to have that city be shorthand for the company the way Stuttgart is for Porsche, but the Neckarsulm plant has roots stretching back to the nineteenth century via NSU, one of the companies that ended up forming Audi's four rings

Launched in 1994, the A8 arrived with aluminum-intensive construction to keep weight down and an available 4.2-liter V8 that still rates as one of the best-sounding engines ever made. It was businesslike, composed with all-wheel-drive for all conditions, managing to be both discreet and muscular, like a bodyguard in a well-tailored suit.

Subsequent generations remained a little more understated than rivals from Mercedes and BMW, but the fifth-gen car that's just exited production was only a year away from celebrating its tenth birthday. Even with a mid-cycle facelift, that's a bit long in the tooth for a flagship.

Taking over flagship duties is Audi's Q9 SUV, a proper three-row family hauler that's aimed at the BMW X7 and Mercedes GLS . The Q9 is certainly large and imposing, and it can carry more passengers and cargo than any A8 model. Does it have that same charisma? Put it this way: Jason Bateman is a very talented actor and producer. He is not Jason Statham.

Meanwhile, Audi may return with some kind of electrified successor to the A8, perhaps as an extended, embiggened version of whatever the new battery-electric A4 ends up looking like. Until then, any Audi-loving underworld soldiers of fortune will have to make do with a brown Mercedes 450 SEL 6.9 and a rocket launcher.

OK, so we've seen that spending time living with an EV , even temporarily, goes a long way to debunking pro-oil propaganda and can change people's minds about whether or not an EV is right for them. Personally, I think the easiest way to make that happen is for owners who want to see EVs get more popular to lend their cars to as many people as they can, for at least 3 days at a time. Ideally, automakers would offer 120-hour test drives to anyone who wants one, but that would be wildly expensive, so I understand why it's hard to even get a 72-hour loan.

Automakers can't sit back here, though. And I'm not just saying that because EVs are the future (they really are), or because I want my nieces and nephews to grow up breathing clean air (I really do). No, it's because they're already shipping EVs to the U.S., and selling more of them would help both sales and profits, while keeping excess inventory from piling up on dealer lots. So here's the idea I'm offering every automaker, free and clear: introduce incentives that encourage dealers to use EVs as service loaners.

When an auto journalist gives business advice, usually, the best thing any automaker can do is the opposite. And that goes double when that advice is on Jalopnik, a site that still loves a good s—post. I'm also well aware I'm not a serious journalist. But tell me the service loaner isn't the most cost-effective way to get customers into an EV long enough for them to realize how great it is to have a gas station in your garage.

I know we all love conquest sales, but current owners are your most likely future customers. The real key to a future EV sale, though, is the low-pressure, no-commitment, just-try-it-for-fun nature of the service loaner. Even people who actively hate EVs would probably be willing to play with one for three or four days while their car's in the shop if the loaner was free. Customers are less likely to think it's some sort of sales trick, too, if the offer comes from a service manager instead of a salesperson.

Considering we're talking about people who already own a car, I don't know if we'd see large numbers of owners picking up their cars, handing over the keys to the loaner EV, and demanding to trade their car in. But as long as you make a good car, there are no downsides to making a positive impression on your customers. And I bet that program would end up being the most cost-effective sales tool in any automaker's arsenal. Not because they're forcing people to go electric but because EVs do such a great job of selling themselves when they fit a prospective owner's lifestyle.

Not everyone can justify an EV. It's pricier and less convenient if you can't charge at home, and some people do crazy amounts of driving or frequent towing. But if you work for an automaker, you know your EVs make better daily drivers for regular homeowners than your most popular daily drivers, and you know they'd sell better if you could get more butts in seats. Now you have a way to get your most likely customers' butts in those seats for far less than the cost of launching a 120-hour test drive program.

Even better, the anti-EV crowd should be all over this one. If EVs are still as bad as they're convinced they are, then a few days driving an EV should be all anyone needs to disabuse them of the notion that they should go electric. Give the skeptics at your company the opportunity to rack up a win and prove this whole EV thing is a waste of everyone's time and money. I mean, they aren't afraid people will like EVs better if they just spend some time with one, are they? Let's put our money where our mouth is and find out.

raw_title: Ford Under Investigation for Airbags that Cause Burn Injuries
title: Ford Under Investigation for Airbags that Cause Burn Injuries
raw_summary: Ford is currently under investigation by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration’s Office of Defects Investigation for more than a million vehicles whose front airbags could cause serious burns. According to the Preliminary Evaluation documents filed with the ODI, the investigation covers an estimated 1,236,155 Ford Explorer SUVs built between the 2021 and 2026 model years. The investigation documents explain that the ODI has received eight Vehicle Owner Questionnaires and four Early Warning Reporting “Death and Injury” reports that include allegations of burn injuries caused by the deployment of the seat-mounted side airbags. In each case, the injuries were limited to the driver, the front passenger, or both; the report didn’t detail any injuries to rear passengers or fatalities of any kind.

title: Nissan Brings The Patrol Name Back To The U.S. After Nearly 60 Years ... Kind Of
raw_summary: In a move that's either pure nostalgia-bait or an appeal to hardcore off-road nerds, Nissan is bringing the Patrol nameplate back to the U.S. for the first time since 1969. No, Nissan's Armada isn't getting a name change. Don't freak out, Armada faithful. Instead, as a celebration for the Patrol's 75th anniversary, Nissan is bringing the name back as a trim level on its full-size SUV brute. Called the Armada Patrol Pro-4X, the body-on-frame SUV adds all sorts of neat off-road extras while also not being terribly different from the normal Pro-4X it replaces, save for new Patrol badging on the tailgate, center console, door sills and floor mats. That's what it's all about, baby. There are also a handful of optional extras, like some very tough-looking Nismo-branded rock sliders and a roof rack with an incorporated light bar, that are new for 2027. They can be had along with Nismo's existing 18-inch Axis wheels, which are wrapped in BF Goodrich All-Terrain T/A K03 rubber.

Under the hood, you'll find the same twin-turbocharged 3.5-liter V6 as the cool normal Armada , pumping out 425 horsepower and 516 pound-feet of torque. It's paired to a nine-speed automatic transmission that sends power to all four wheels courtesy of a full-time 4WD system and a locking rear differential. To help keep you out of trouble when you're off-road, the Patrol Pro-4X comes with height-adjustable air suspension, underbody armor, and tow hooks.

If you're the type of person who is a real nasty Nissan nerd, or you just love off-roading, perhaps the 2027 Armada Patrol Pro-4X is for you. If that's the case, you've just got to be ready to fork over $81,265, including $2,275 destination. That's no small chunk of change, but it actually undercuts this car's closest rival, the Toyota Sequoia TRD Pro , by $6,855.

I won't lie to ya, I don't completely understand the decision here for Nissan. I mean, Patrol is hardly an established nameplate in the U.S. It only existed here from 1962 to 1969, and it's been gone for a hell of a long time, so I can't imagine there's a ton of nostalgia behind it. I suppose you could point to an appeal to off-roading nerds as a reason for the name addition or perhaps Nissan is getting ready to switch the Armada's name over to Patrol in the U.S., though I sort of doubt that.

Patrol has been a part of Nissan since 1951, so there's obviously a lot of brand heritage behind it. I'm just not sure there's a lot of brand heritage behind it in the U.S. Better late than never, though, and Patrol Pro-4X does sound a bit cooler than just Pro-4X, so who am I to complain?

article_paragraphs: Chinese automaker BYD is stepping into the ultra-luxury space with its Yangwang brand, and its latest car, the Altior, features coach doors, reclining rear seats, an incredibly smooth ride, and even umbrellas that pop out of the door panels. Sound familiar? Yeah, it looks like BYD is gunning for the Rolls-Royce Phantom’s spot as the ultimate luxury sedan.

Though closer in size to the Rolls-Royce Ghost , the Altior, which means “higher” in Latin, aims to offer an elevated passenger experience rooted in Chinese tradition. Wolfgang Egger, BYD’s design director, says the Altior was inspired by the “ding,” ancient bronze cauldrons that symbolize strength, dignity, and harmony. Even the air vents have cultural significance, featuring inlays of yellow Hetian jade, which is traditionally associated with wealth, prosperity, and authority. Still, there’s more than a hint of Phantom to the exterior styling.

Jade air vents are just the tip of the Altior-sized iceberg, though. In total, the interior features 48 decorative jewelry-inspired controls. Occupants will be swaddled in full-grain leather, complemented by an ancient embroidery style that splits silk threads to create cloud-like motifs. Wool floor mats and natural wood trim round out the interior materials. Outside, the ornate grille is crafted to highlight reflecting light, and the sides of the car feature a contrasting black roof, silver accents, and sleek 21-inch wheels.

Rear zero-gravity massaging seats recline for a truly knock-out ride, especially when paired with the Altior’s relaxation mode that lowers the sun blinds, lifts the leg rests, and softens the cabin’s ambient lighting. Pair that with a 39-speaker Dynaudio sound system and a 21.4-inch overhead screen for perhaps the most exciting way to join a conference call ever invented. There are also two refrigerators—one in the front and one in the rear that can also keep things warm.

A quad-motor electric architecture powers the Altior, with each motor powering a wheel independently. An active body control system can adjust the car’s suspension in real time depending on road conditions to offer a smooth ride no matter where it’s going. BYD claims the Altior will have a range of about 621 miles on a single charge and promises speedy recharging times. Specific information about charging rates and power output hasn’t been released yet.

Yangwang seems pretty confident in the Altior’s safety system, calling it “God’s Eye.” The software includes navigation assistance on highway routes, urban streets, and from one parking spot to another. It’ll also apparently be able to float if it hits water and do a tank turn, though both of those seem to only be useful in situations that a luxury sedan likely will never find itself in.

These luxury beasts won’t reach U.S. roads, but they’re currently available for pre-order in China and are slated to start at the equivalent of around $311,540. BYD plans to bring the Altior to parts of Europe in the future.

Alayna Wilkening grew up reading motorsport magazines and following her grandpa around his Chevrolet dealership's showroom floor. In true Hoosier fashion, her first car was a hot pink custom cardboard "Fiero-vette" for her kindergarten Kindy 500 race. She now autocrosses a 1994 Miata with her dad, which she learned to drive the night before her first event. Alayna went to Indiana University and graduated with a degree in journalism and a minor in graphic design. As a testament to her great taste in cars, her first real one was a metallic orange 2007 Chevy HHR, which she lovingly called "The Dumptruck."

But for 2027, Vespa has given its electric lineup a fairly significant technological overhaul while leaving that iconic steel bodywork largely untouched.

article_paragraphs: Vespa’s electric scooters have never exactly screamed for attention. That’s sort of the point. They look like Vespas, ride like Vespas, and just happen to swap the gasoline engine for a much quieter electric drivetrain.
But for 2027, Vespa has given its electric lineup a fairly significant technological overhaul while leaving that iconic steel bodywork largely untouched.

Unveiled at EICMA 2026 in Milan, the new electric Vespa lineup now consists of the Primavera Elettrica, Sprint S Elettrica, and the faster Primavera Tech Elettrica. And while you’d be forgiven for struggling to spot the differences from across the show floor, there’s a lot more happening underneath.

The biggest upgrade is an entirely new electric motor developed and manufactured in Italy by Vespa parent company Piaggio Group. The motor uses a new modular design intended to improve both performance and efficiency, while also doing away with rare-earth materials.
On the 45 km/h (28 mph) Primavera and Sprint S models, Vespa says the new motor provides stronger acceleration for stop-and-go city riding. Range reaches up to 85 km (53 miles) in Eco mode.

But perhaps the biggest practical improvement is the new removable battery. Being able to pull the battery out of the scooter and carry it inside for charging makes a massive difference for urban riders who don’t have access to a garage or dedicated charging spot – exactly the kind of riders Vespa is targeting.

The Primavera Tech is where things get a little faster. This version is homologated as a motorcycle rather than a moped in Europe and reaches 67 km/h (42 mph). That’s still not terribly fast, but the electric Vespa line has never been known for its top speed.
Its range has increased by 12.5% thanks to the new motor and Vehicle Management System, reaching 90 km (56 miles) on the WMTC cycle or up to 100 km (62 miles) in Eco mode.

raw_summary: Looks like the Xtreme is more than just a badge and sticker package China's automakers are in a record-breaking mood. article_paragraphs: Looks like the Xtreme is more than just a badge and sticker package

China's automakers are in a record-breaking mood. Last week, BYD became the first to smash the 500 kmh barrier with a production car when its Yangwang U9 Xtreme hit 313 mph (503 kmh) on a public highway in Abu Dhabi. And now it looks like its rival Xiaomi could be about to declare a new EV lap record at Germany's Nürburgring.

Our spy photo team snapped a fully camouflaged SU7 Ultra with a massive GT3-style rear wing putting in some hot laps at the Ring in October, and now another Ultra prototype is busting the same moves, only this time minus the disguise.

Losing the swirly wrap gives us our best look yet at the most aggressive car Xiaomi has made, including all of the other aero parts that complement the big swan-neck rear spoiler. That wing naturally draws your attention, but there's plenty more going on, including a new front bumper, big splitter, and a set of louvers in the front fenders, mounted directly above the wheels. Porsche fits similar parts to the fenders of its 911 GT3 RS to get rid of air pressure that builds up inside the front wheel arches, and it's very likely Xiaomi has the same idea.

And that's not the only GT3 RS idea Xiaomi appears to have appropriated. The SU7's front fenders are cut inwards in front of the door, just like on the hot 911. Likewise, the rear fenders cut inward after the rear wheels, exposing some of the fat trackday rubber wrapped around the double-five-spoke wheels. We'd also be very surprised if that rear wing didn't have some kind of F1-style DRS (drag-reduction system) technology.

The SU7 did briefly hold the lap record for production sedans and EVs after an Ultra lapped the 12.8-mile (20.6 km) forest track in 7:04.957 in June 2025. That rapid run put it 0.3 seconds ahead of the Rimac Nevera hypercar, and over 2.5 seconds clear of the Porsche Taycan Turbo GT. A massive power advantage was central to Xiaomi's success. The SU7 makes 1,526 hp (1,138 kW / 1,548 PS) for brief periods, but the Taycan's push-to-pass attack mode only gives 939 hp (700 kW / 952 PS).

Porsche wasn't about to let an upstart smartphone manufacturer snatch its title and get away with it, though. The German brand returned to the Ring in May of this year with a Taycan Turbo GT modified in conjunction with Manthey . The package included front and rear aero components, road-legal track tires, lighter wheels, and a tweaked bi-motor electric powertrain.

The Manthey Taycan still only makes 978hp (730 kW / 992 PS) in attack mode, which is well below the SU7's output, but that didn't hold the Taycan back. It lapped the Ring in 6:55.553, becoming the first EV and sedan to dip into the sixes. And now it's Xiaomi's turn to reply.

Oil prices fell sharply Monday, with Brent crude dropping more than 3% to below $95 a barrel after President Trump downplayed the prospect of further U.S. attacks on Iran, even as attacks on Saudi Arabia and fresh incidents involving tankers in the Strait of Hormuz highlighted continuing risks to Middle Eastern oil supplies.

Trump said in an interview with CNN Sunday that further U.S. strikes on Iran were highly unlikely as long as negotiations over Tehran's nuclear program and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz made progress. His comments followed a sharp decline in oil prices last week as traders assessed the prospects for a diplomatic resolution following the Democratic Party's victory in the U.S. midterm elections.

Saudi Arabia is still dealing with its Houthi problem, and that could always derail a peace deal. Especially since Houthi attacks struck Riyadh, hitting an Aramco administrative building but not killing anyone. Additionally, projectiles hit at least one, if not two ships in the area over the weekend. So there's still more to work on, but these days, we'll take any positive sign we can get.

Of course, while this year's midterm election proved to be the biggest win for Democrats since Watergate, Democrats won't take control of Congress until new members are sworn in next year, and they won't have a chance at the White House until the 2028 election. With both the House and Senate, they'll have the power to check Trump and Republicans, but there are still limits on what they can do while Trump's president. As a result, don't expect a peace deal overnight, even if gas gets cheaper. From the WSJ:

However, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said talks with Washington had made no progress and Tehran was waiting to see whether the U.S. administration would change its position following the elections.

Signs of easing supply tightness are also emerging in the oil market. The spread between the nearest Brent futures contracts has narrowed to around $2.60 a barrel from nearly $4 at the end of last week, while physical crude prices are trading below futures, according to MUFG.

The Mustang Mach-E went on sale in late 2020 as Ford’s first fully electric crossover SUV designed from the ground up.
Since launching the 2021 Mustang Mach-E, Ford has been collecting data from over 36,000 vehicles that have traveled two billion miles across the US and Canada.
According to Ford, the Mach-E’s battery has retained 92% of its health on average over the past five years.

Across its full EV lineup, including the F-150 Lightning and E-Transit, Ford said its battery packs maintain more than 90% health on average after 100,000 miles. The key number to look at is the spread, with 95% of vehicles falling between 87% and 97% health.

Of 2021 model-year EV owners, Ford said, more than 2,000 have crossed 100,000 miles with their original battery averaging better than 91% health, while over 30 have crossed the 200,000-mile mark and average 88% health.
Ford is using real-world data to help owners take good care of their electric vehicles, no matter how much they know about batteries and other EV tech.
It’s also applying lessons from developing the Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform, which will underpin its next-generation EVs, starting with the Fantom pickup next year.

raw_summary: West Yorkshire has made two substantial commitments to its bus network. article_paragraphs: West Yorkshire has made two substantial commitments to its bus network. On November 2, FirstGroup announced a £109 million agreement with the West Yorkshire Combined Authority covering five depots, associated infrastructure and 330 buses, including 79 battery-electric vehicles. The authority is also spending £120 million on more than 250 new buses through a separate programme. These investments will help establish the region’s new franchised Weaver Network, but many of the assets being acquired will remain in use long after the first operating contracts have ended.

West Yorkshire’s fleet and depot commitments illustrate a problem explored in my 83-page report, The Bus Is Not the System . The accompanying TFIE Strategy Briefing assessment examines which decisions are becoming expensive to reverse and what authorities should establish before making their next commitments.

The Weaver Network changes the relationship between public transport planning and private bus operations. The Combined Authority will specify services and retain responsibility for passenger revenue under its initial large contracts, while private operators deliver the routes. The region is securing assets that will remain important regardless of which company operates the buses. In principle, that can make future competition easier because bidders do not each have to provide a new depot and fleet.

The challenge is that buses, operating contracts and infrastructure follow different clocks. An operating contract might last five or seven years. Vehicles can work through successive contracts, while depot buildings and electrical connections may remain useful for decades. A change in route patterns, population or employment locations can make an established depot less convenient. A bus can often be reassigned, but a multi-megawatt electricity connection cannot be transferred to another site because the network needs charging capacity elsewhere.

West Yorkshire has arranged a staged transition. The five depot sales have completed, while the buses are scheduled to transfer as new franchises begin operating between May 2027 and October 2028. First Bus will continue delivering existing services under temporary depot leases and will manage electrification at Bradford and Huddersfield, with the authority paying for that work. The arrangements allow services and infrastructure development to proceed while ownership and operating responsibilities change.

Securing strategically important depots is a defensible approach. It reduces dependence on an incumbent operator’s control of scarce infrastructure and can help new companies compete for future contracts. The authority also assumes long-term responsibilities for the assets, including maintenance, future electrical capacity and their suitability for a changing passenger network. A depot can be worth purchasing without every potential alternative having been examined, but the consequences of losing those alternatives should be understood before the agreement becomes binding.

Electrification makes this especially important. Charging equipment, substations and electricity connections involve different suppliers, construction schedules and contractual responsibilities from the buses themselves. Vehicle orders can proceed before chargers are fully commissioned when the infrastructure delivery pathway is sufficiently assured. Problems arise when a fleet commitment depends on electrical capacity that cannot be delivered in time, or when the fallback arrangements are inadequate.

The passenger network can also change in ways that alter the original investment case. Better bus priority can reduce the number of vehicles needed to maintain a timetable. New housing developments can shift demand toward different corridors. A major employment centre or hospital relocation can change the value of existing routes and depots. The infrastructure secured today should support those possibilities rather than make sensible network improvements prohibitively expensive.

title: Uber launches parking service following SpotHero acquisition, with an eye on robotaxis
raw_summary: Uber on Monday said it is launching a new service that lets customers reserve and pay for parking in major U.S. cities, about nine months after the ride-hailing company acquired parking app SpotHero. The acquisition, announced back in February, gives Uber access to a network of 13,000 garages, lots and valet services across more than 400 cities, the company said. And while Uber’s initial plans will focus on human drivers, the company also plans to leverage these parking spots to help the dozens of autonomous vehicle companies it has partnered with.

article_paragraphs: Uber on Monday said it is launching a new service that lets customers reserve and pay for parking in major U.S. cities, about nine months after the ride-hailing company acquired parking app SpotHero.

The acquisition, announced back in February, gives Uber access to a network of 13,000 garages, lots and valet services across more than 400 cities, the company said. And while Uber’s initial plans will focus on human drivers, the company also plans to leverage these parking spots to help the dozens of autonomous vehicle companies it has partnered with.

Uber said the parking spots could be used as staging and waiting locations for autonomous vehicles to help reduce congestion and deadheading, which refers to the miles a vehicle travels without a paying passenger or cargo on board.

For now, the company plans to focus on commuters driving their own vehicles. Uber said it will initially launch in 15 U.S. cities, including Atlanta, Austin, Boston, Chicago, Dallas, Denver, Los Angeles, Miami, Nashville, New York City, Philadelphia, San Diego, San Francisco, Seattle, and Washington, DC.
Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi indicated earlier this month that the company wants the app to be more relevant to commuters.

“Commute is one of our largest categories,” he said during Uber’s third-quarter earnings call. “And to be able to offer commuters an Uber to work, a pass to avoid surge, and parking if they want it when they want to drive is a great example of us building out our inventory of services to the commuter who is a top customer for us.”

The parking service is the latest in a series of efforts at Uber to build an ecosystem of products that keep customers engaged with its app for everything from hailing a ride and ordering food and groceries, to packing delivery, renting cars, booking hotels , and connecting users with public transit and robotaxis.

Uber’s membership program, called Uber One, is a key part of that strategy. Uber One attracts subscribers by offering rewards and credits, perks that have helped the program grow to more than 55 million members as of September 30. For instance, Uber is offering members a chance to earn 10% back in credits on eligible parking reservations. Those credits can later be used for rides and Uber Eats orders.

Now, it appears that Toyota is following that lead and giving the RAV4 Woodland more than just all-terrain tires. Upon its debut, the biggest change, other than some body cladding, was that the all-terrain tires it came with boosted its ride height.
article_paragraphs: A little over a year ago, Toyota debuted its latest RAV4 . For the first time, it became available in trims like GR Sport and Woodland. Now, the latter is getting a serious update for 2027. Upon its debut, the biggest change, other than some body cladding, was that the all-terrain tires it came with boosted its ride height. That's not all that shocking. We just got back from testing the new Hyundai Palisade XRT Pro , and that company admitted early on that its XRT products were mostly appearance packages.

Since then, Hyundai's been working hard to incorporate hardware to back up the badge and the styling. Now, it appears that Toyota is following that lead and giving the RAV4 Woodland more than just all-terrain tires. In fact, after looking at all of these changes, it wouldn't be shocking if some of the earliest buyers of the new RAV4 feel a little green with envy.

It's one thing to look off-road ready and another to actually have the hardware to back it up. For 2027, the RAV4 Woodland gets more of the latter, starting with new springs and shocks that boost total ground clearance from 8.5 inches — on the prior version — to 9.1. In addition, there are new jounce bumpers so at full suspension compression, bottoming out isn't as harsh in the cabin or on the components.

On top of that, there are software changes worth noting. Last year, the Woodland had a Trail mode. That's gone now, and instead, drivers have more granular control via two new modes: 'Rock & Dirt' and 'Mud & Sand'. Being able to tell the car what type of ground it's on is a nice addition, though Hyundai is working to give the task to AI . Finally, the entire fleet of 2027 PHEV RAV4s, including the Woodland, gets a NACS port, DC fast-charging, and an 11-kW onboard charger.

Previously, the Woodland and XSE offered this onboard charger and DC charging, but now, it's included across the lineup. Speaking of the PHEV drivetrain, it continues with the same 321-horsepower 2.5-liter four-cylinder that it did last year. Toyota says it'll achieve up to 38 mpg in the city, 35 mpg on the highway, and 37 mpg combined for the Woodland. The SE is rated for up to 42, 39, and 41 mpg, respectively. Each PHEV offers at least 45 miles of all-electric range when fully charged.

raw_title: Honda Announces Plans to Build a New $3 Billion Factory in Ohio
title: Honda Announces Plans to Build a New $3 Billion Factory in Ohio
raw_summary: Honda is already well entrenched in Ohio. The Japanese automaker has two vehicle assembly factories in the state, in East Liberty and Marysville, along with the Anna Engine Plant and a transmission facility in Russells Point. Now Honda is taking its commitment to Ohio even further, announcing today a plant to build a new factory in Central Ohio and to invest $3 billion into the project. The new factory will be located near Honda’s existing manufacturing facilities, on land between the East Liberty and Marysville plants. Production is set to kick off in 2029, and the factory will have a planned capacity of 240,000 vehicles, boosting Honda’s U.S. production capacity to around 1.3 million vehicles per year. The new factory will create over 2000 new jobs, Honda says. Honda didn’t specify what would be built at the new factory but did say it would be capable of producing everything from gas-powered models to hybrids and full EVs.

The new factory will be located near Honda’s existing manufacturing facilities, on land between the East Liberty and Marysville plants. Production is set to kick off in 2029, and the factory will have a planned capacity of 240,000 vehicles, boosting Honda’s U.S. production capacity to around 1.3 million vehicles per year. The new factory will create over 2000 new jobs, Honda says. Honda didn’t specify what would be built at the new factory but did say it would be capable of producing everything from gas-powered models to hybrids and full EVs.

The new factory is just one part of an increased investment in hybrid vehicles from Honda. The company is also investing in its factory in Lincoln, Alabama, planning to increase production capacity and expand engine production to include a new V-6 hybrid powertrain. Honda says the plant will also get more flexible, by being able to build multiple models on the two vehicle production lines. The Anna Engine Plant, meanwhile, is undergoing a substantial retooling in order to produce a next-generation Atkinson-cycle four-cylinder engine for upcoming compact and midsize models.

Honda’s transmission factory in Ohio is also getting retooled, with an existing transmission production line set to become a second production line for next-generation hybrid systems bound for compact and midsize vehicles. The facility will also lead the way on Honda’s hybrid system for larger vehicles, which will also be produced at Honda’s transmission factory in Georgia. More details on the vehicles that will use these new hybrid systems should emerge over the next couple of years.

raw_title: Musk admits Tesla doesn’t have enough talent to build more than one car at a time after exodus
title: Musk admits Tesla doesn't have enough talent to build more than one car at a time after exodus
raw_summary: Elon Musk now says Tesla can’t build the Cybertruck and the Cybercab at the same time because there are only so many “smart, dedicated people” to go around. Half the executives he showed off in 2023 as proof of Tesla’s “bench strength” have since left the company. It’s the most honest explanation yet for how Tesla went from five consumer vehicle programs at the start of 2026 to a single platform, Model 3 and Model Y, by the middle of 2027.

article_paragraphs: Elon Musk now says Tesla can’t build the Cybertruck and the Cybercab at the same time because there are only so many “smart, dedicated people” to go around. Half the executives he showed off in 2023 as proof of Tesla’s “bench strength” have since left the company.
It’s the most honest explanation yet for how Tesla went from five consumer vehicle programs at the start of 2026 to a single platform, Model 3 and Model Y, by the middle of 2027.

On Friday, Musk said Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas around the middle of next year “to make room for increased Cybercab production.” As we pointed out at the time , Giga Texas isn’t short on space. The Cybertruck line runs at a fraction of its installed capacity because the truck sells a fraction of what Tesla planned.
A day later, replying to a user on X, Musk gave a different reason:
“The biggest thing most people fail to understand is that there are a very limited number of smart, dedicated people! They can only do so many things.”
He added that if Tesla has to “maintain a complex production line, supply chain and allocate engineering for Cybertruck, we can’t use those people” for scaling Cybercab.

By this morning, the explanation had shifted again, to the “opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck.” But the Saturday version is the one that matters. Musk is telling us the bottleneck at Tesla isn’t factory space or money. It’s people.

The Cybertruck is the second casualty this year. In January, Musk announced the end of the Model S and Model X on Tesla’s Q4 earnings call and summed up the reason in one word: “Autonomy.” The Fremont line is being converted to build Optimus robots, and by April, only inventory was left .

The new model is expected to slot between the Dark Horse and the Dark Horse SC, and it is likely to adopt a similar naming structure, instead of reviving the Shelby badge. According to the report, the new version will be a track-focused trim with commensurate cooling and braking capabilities, as well as a wide-body style similar to that of the Dark Horse SC.

Rather than utilizing the supercharged 5.2-liter V-8 found in the SC, Ford is expected to give the GT350 successor a naturally aspirated mill. Exact power figures are up in the air, but the door has been left open for the return of the 5.2-liter flat-plane-crank Voodoo engine. When Ford retired the Voodoo in 2020, the high-revving engine produced 526 horsepower, a figure that slots neatly between the Dark Horse’s 500-hp Coyote 5.0-liter V-8 and the 795 ponies on offer from the Dark Horse SC’s supercharged 5.2. Assuming Ford does bring back the Voodoo, there’s also every chance that the company will have scraped together a few more horsepower for the engine. In any event, the new model is expected to come mated to a six-speed Tremec manual gearbox, though an automatic gearbox could be available as well.

Exact timing of the rumored model’s arrival remains a mystery, but Ford Authority’s sources told the outlet that the car will become available in 2027 and will be offered as a 2027 model. Car and Driver reached out to Ford for comment on the report. We will update this story if we hear back.

title: Mitsubishi Pajero Prepares For The Outback With Factory-Backed Accessories
raw_summary: The reborn Mitsubishi Pajero is heading to Australian dealerships next month and the company has already announced a lineup of factory-backed accessories. These were developed for the harsh conditions of the outback, with input from Aussie engineers. According to the local arm of Mitsubishi, work on the genuine accessory program started in early 2022, far before the new Pajero was unveiled in September 2026. This was made possible by granting the Australian team early access to CAD data, before the first Pajero prototypes were built for testing. The digital collaboration included local companies and was followed by visits at the Okazaki R&D facility in Japan. Thanks to this early integration, the new Pajero already had mounting points and pre-wiring structures compatible with protection bars and towing equipment. It allowed Mitsubishi to offer 20 accessories for the Pajero available at launch.

This was made possible by granting the Australian team early access to CAD data, before the first Pajero prototypes were built for testing. The digital collaboration included local companies and was followed by visits at the Okazaki R&D facility in Japan. Thanks to this early integration, the new Pajero already had mounting points and pre-wiring structures compatible with protection bars and towing equipment. It allowed Mitsubishi to offer 20 accessories for the Pajero available at launch.

Steve Pearson, Engineering Manager for Accessory Development in Mitsubishi Motors Australia who led the program said in a press release that their goal was to cater to the specific needs of local buyers. "Australians ask a lot of their four-wheel drives. They tow caravans, travel off-road and cover enormous distances, so our accessories must be more than cosmetic additions. They need to be engineered as part of the vehicle experience."

The highlight of the catalog is the Front Protection Bar (FPB) which is available in steel hooped and hoopless versions. This covers the entire front end of the Pajero, protecting the grille and headlights from road debris and minor collisions, though it is not as imposing as the massive bull bar on Toyota's RAV4 . The FPB was specifically designed not to interfere with the ADAS sensors of the ladder-frame SUV.

More discreet options for protecting the bodywork include clear headlight protectors, hood protectors with a clear, tinted or matte black finish, a nudge bar with a black or polished finish, a skid plate, and rock sliders. Owners can also upgrade the Pajero with a snorkel, auxiliary LED lights, and a roof rack. Another important accessory for Australians is the tow bar, which is mounted to the ladder frame chassis with special reinforcements. This can be combined with a towbar harness, an electric brake harness, and a weight distribution hitch. Finally, a heavy-duty winch cradle will help get the Pajero unstuck when there's no one around.

The new Pajero rides on a ladder-frame chassis derived from the Triton pickup, albeit with a model-specific suspension setup and greater refinement. Under the hood lies a turbodiesel 2.4-liter four-cylinder engine generating 201 horsepower (150 kW/204 PS) and 480 Nm (354 lb-ft) of torque. An eight-speed automatic gearbox sends power to all four wheels via Mitsubishi's Super Select 4WD-II system paired with Super All-Wheel Control.

In Australia, the Pajero is priced from AU$68,490 ($47,000) for the entry-level five-seat GLS trim, and tops out at AU$84,990 ($58,400) for the flagship GSR. The cost of the factory-backed accessories will be announced at a later date. Those who make an early reservation will receive three years of complimentary servicing and $1,000 worth of accessories. The optional bits fitted prior to delivery carry the standard 5-year/100,000 km warranty, which expands to 10 years and 200,000 km when the SUV is maintained through the official dealer service network. Mitsubishi has not shared plans of bringing the Pajero to North America, although it will be exported to certain global markets with the Montero nameplate.

article_paragraphs: On the Monday after the Formula 1 Brazilian Grand Prix, Oscar Piastri and Mark Webber announced in a joint statement that the latter and Ann Neal would no longer manage the 25-year-old McLaren driver. The timing may come as a surprise – now rather than at the end of the season – but the news itself had been on the cards for some time.

The clearest hint came from Piastri during pre-season testing in Bahrain. While this writer was mainly interested in his opinion of the 2026 cars – which immediately brought a telling smile to Piastri's face – an Australian colleague raised the subject of Webber's changing role.

"There wasn't anything specific, we just made a decision for things to look a bit different," Piastri said on that unusually cold February evening in the Bahrain paddock. "Mark is still very much involved and I've been in contact with him a lot over the last few weeks. He just won't be trackside as much anymore. So that's really the extent of it. There was nothing specific that triggered it."

Although that last point is essentially true, it is clear that the 2025 season was intense on several fronts – including behind the scenes, at least from Webber’s perspective. That was naturally closely linked to the 'papaya rules' through which McLaren tried to treat both drivers as fairly as possible, but which also made life difficult for the team at certain moments, as Andrea Stella frankly admitted at the beginning of this year.

It is no secret that Webber was not always happy with how McLaren handled certain moments on track, nor with the explanation for Piastri's dip in form during the final quarter of the season, which ultimately cost him the world title. It is important to emphasise, however, that a manager's role is also to defend the interests of his own driver, even though there are multiple ways of doing so.

Webber naturally had the experiences from his own Red Bull years in mind and wanted to prevent Piastri from ever being labelled a number two driver in the F1 paddock. In a recent interview with Autosport, former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner even described this as a key part of Webber's mentality, a worldview that Horner believes he brought into the cockpit.

"I think probably the difficulty with Mark was, he motivated himself through adversity. He always drove better when he felt that the world was against him," Horner said. "He could see this talent emerging in Sebastian [Vettel], and he was using everything in his locker to try and destabilise that, or to cause any tension in a way that would then fall back in his favour. I think as a team we were learning how to handle these dynamics."

title: This BMW i7 Prototype Is Alpina's First EV
raw_summary: It's missing the signature tailpipes, but it should still be lightning quick BMW took full control of Alpina at the start of 2026, and it's got big plans to push the brand down unfamiliar roads. article_paragraphs: It's missing the signature tailpipes, but it should still be lightning quick

BMW took full control of Alpina at the start of 2026, and it's got big plans to push the brand down unfamiliar roads. One of those is the world of fully electric cars, and these spy shots show what could be the first-ever EV to wear the Alpina badge.

We've already had an official look at a camouflaged prototype of the upcoming combustion BMW Alpina 7 Series sedan. BMW dropped pictures of that one last week, along with the promise that it would do more than 186 mph (300 kmh), probably courtesy of a tuned version of the 563 horsepower (570 PS), 4.4-liter V8 fitted to the BMW M760 xDrive. And in a similar vein, this electric version looks set to take its lead from the i7 M70 xDrive.

Visually, there's not much to separate this electric Alpina prototype from the combustion one seen earlier. Both have the same razor-thin LED DRLs that are mounted separately from the main headlight units. They also share the same lower bumper shape and grille outline. But this new EV's grille is blanked off, whereas the ICE sedan has a full set of horizontal bars and mesh behind them, allowing air to feed the V8's radiator.

This EV even rides on the exact same wheels as the combustion Alpina 7 Series prototype our spy team snapped last month, but there's one very obvious difference at the back. The gas car has a pair of oval exhaust tailpipes at each corner – an Alpina trademark – and the EV has none.

BMW facelifted the i7 earlier this year, and later added 20 hp (20 PS) to the top trim's dual-motor powertrain. That boosted the i7 M70 xDrive to 670 hp (680 PS), and although the torque figure didn't change, there was already plenty on hand.

Launch control gives M70 drivers 811 lb-ft (1,100 Nm), which is enough for a zero to 62 mph (100 kmh) time of 3.8 seconds. Alpinas have long prioritized effortless pace over raw sports car performance, so that kind of urge, while not record-setting by EV standards, might be enough to keep its customers happy. But at the same time, those Alpina customers have grown to expect that their cars are more than BMWs with an extra helping of leather, so don't rule out a horsepower increase, and a tenth or two sliced off that sixty time.

Additional interior luxury is still a key part of an Alpina's appeal, though, so we can be sure that BMW will be putting plenty of effort into that department. And like every new 7 Series, Alpina's i7 will come with BMW's new Panoramic iDrive digital display and tablet touchscreen. It will also get the same 112.5 kWh battery pack, which now employs BMW's round cell technology. Adopting them lifted the M70's range to 426 miles (686 km), and the Alpina should be in the same ballpark.

title: The Mazda 2 Is Dead, But Something Else Is Taking Its Place
raw_summary: While the world was expecting the Mazda 2 to enter a new generation in the coming years, the automaker has confirmed it will be phased out and replaced by a different model. According to Mazda, the long-serving supermini will give way to the next-generation CX-3 subcompact crossover, with the two lines effectively merging into one. The announcement was part of Mazda's Integrated Report for 2026, which is currently available only in Japanese. Within the official PDF file, Chief Technology Officer Ryuichi Umeshita outlined the transition for Mazda's entry-level products: "In 2027, we plan to introduce the next-generation Mazda CX-3, produced at our plant in Thailand, to the Japanese and ASEAN markets. It will expand Mazda's value as a new-era entry model, replacing the Mazda 2."

Within the official PDF file, Chief Technology Officer Ryuichi Umeshita outlined the transition for Mazda's entry-level products: "In 2027, we plan to introduce the next-generation Mazda CX-3, produced at our plant in Thailand, to the Japanese and ASEAN markets. It will expand Mazda's value as a new-era entry model, replacing the Mazda 2."

The next generation of the CX-3 was confirmed in Mazda's mid-year financial report in August 2026, although the company had shown official sketches of a subcompact crossover in February 2025. The latest report reveals it will come fitted with a mild-hybrid powertrain, although technical specifications about the engine displacement and output are still under wraps.

The CX-3 will adopt Mazda's evolved styling language, inspired by the Vision X-Compact concept that debuted at the Japan Mobility Show in late 2025. The hatchback-style stance and tiny footprint of the concept tricked the world into believing it was going to evolve into a new Mazda 2. However, it now seems that the higher-margin crossover is the one that got the green light for production.

The official sketches suggest that the CX-3 will borrow a few styling features from the much larger CX-5 , albeit in a much chunkier and slightly sportier way. We also expect it to gain the latest technology Mazda has to offer in terms of infotainment and driving assistance.

As with the current generation, the next CX-3 will be manufactured at the AutoAlliance Thailand (AAT) facility, following a 5 billion baht ($150 million) investment. The subcompact SUV will be sold in Japan, ASEAN regions, and additional global markets. Europe is possible, although North America will likely stick to the larger CX-30 as the entry point in the Mazda lineup.

Earlier this year, leaked documents from Japan indicated that Mazda was planning to end production of the current Mazda 2 and CX-3 before the end of 2026. The mechanically related models have been around largely unchanged since 2014, although Mazda tried to keep them relevant with subtle facelifts and technological updates.

Despite the Mazda2's upcoming global sunset, the Australian division of the brand is determined to keep offering it in local dealerships. As reported by Drive , a Mazda Australia spokesperson said that sales of the Mazda 2 Down Under will continue "well into the future", which effectively means for as long as factory allocations permit. Note that Australia never got the much newer Mazda 2 Hybrid , which is a rebadged version of the Toyota Yaris, exclusively available in Europe and the UK.

raw_title: Chery Says North America Is So Important It Could Build Cars In Canada
title: Chery Says North America Is So Important It Could Build Cars In Canada
raw_summary: Several major Chinese car manufacturers are venturing into the Canadian market thanks to the latest trade deal between the two nations. Chery is one of them, and alongside a plan to launch its vehicles in Canada next year, the company has expressed interest in building its cars locally. Canada's deal with China allows 49,000 Chinese-made EVs and hybrids to be imported into the country at a reduced tariff rate, and companies including BYD, Geely, and Chery, are jumping at the chance. While Chery appears even more eager to expand into the United States than into Canada, it believes having a factory in Canada is a good idea. "Even without the American market, Canada is a market that is worth having a factory for manufacturing," Chery's executive vice president Guibing Zhang said in an interview with Bloomberg . "We are looking for the suitable opportunity and communicating on the possible formats." The easiest way to make this happen would be to find a local manufacturing plant that has free capacity.
summary: Several major Chinese car manufacturers are venturing into the Canadian market thanks to the latest trade deal between the two nations. Chery is one of them, and alongside a plan to launch its vehicles in Canada next year, the company has expressed interest in building its cars locally.
article_paragraphs: Several major Chinese car manufacturers are venturing into the Canadian market thanks to the latest trade deal between the two nations. Chery is one of them, and alongside a plan to launch its vehicles in Canada next year, the company has expressed interest in building its cars locally. Canada's deal with China allows 49,000 Chinese-made EVs and hybrids to be imported into the country at a reduced tariff rate, and companies including BYD, Geely, and Chery, are jumping at the chance.

While Chery appears even more eager to expand into the United States than into Canada, it believes having a factory in Canada is a good idea. "Even without the American market, Canada is a market that is worth having a factory for manufacturing," Chery's executive vice president Guibing Zhang said in an interview with Bloomberg . "We are looking for the suitable opportunity and communicating on the possible formats." The easiest way to make this happen would be to find a local manufacturing plant that has free capacity.

Zhang indicated that Chery is already doing this and has started speaking to investors across Canada who are excited about Chinese car manufacturers . An alternative would be to construct a local plant. However, this would be expensive and wouldn't make sense unless the import quota was raised significantly or the cap was scrapped entirely. Chery currently only fights over a share of 49,000 vehicles so there's no need for it to invest billions of dollars into a new factory, at least for now.

In other markets, Chery has already shown a willingness to work alongside legacy brands. The Chinese automaker has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Nissan in the UK to possibly build vehicles at its Sunderland site. Additionally, Chery runs an ex-Nissan factory in South Africa and will start building its own vehicles there. Although the Canadian government has opened its arms to Chinese vehicles, it doesn't want companies simply building so-called 'knockdown kits' in the country that are built elsewhere, partially disassembled, and then shipped over for reassembly by local workers.

Earlier this year, a report indicated Stellantis was considering doing this with EVs from Leapmotor. This prompted fiery responses from Canada's federal Industry Minister Melanie Joly and Ontario Premier Doug Ford. "These vehicles are completely manufactured in China with Chinese components, then partially disassembled and brought here to be reassembled by several hundred workers, like IKEA furniture kits," noted Automotive Parts Manufacturers' Association president Flavio Volpe during an interview with CTV News . "That's completely different from making cars here and buying $3-billion worth of parts a year in Canada and employing 10,000 to 12,000 employees."

Right around the turn of the century, my wife and I had to pick up our stepdaughter at Chicago Midway Airport so she could come home after spending Christmas with her bio-dad.
Nothing majorly bad happened to us, but it was a very white-knuckle drive.
A huge blizzard hit in the morning when we were supposed to leave. Bio-dad said her flight still hadn't been canceled, so we set off on our way (early, of course).
What normally would have been a 2-hour trip turned into a 4-hour one. Literally, when we got off the highway at our exit to go to Midway, he calls and says her flight was canceled.

So we turned around and headed back home. That was a 6-hour trip going about 30 MPH the whole way. That was the worst because I was really tired by then. It was dark by that point, so you really couldn't see anything but the snow coming down. My mind kept seeing cars spin out in front of me, when they weren't.
We made it almost all the way home but got stuck in the middle of the road about 3 miles from home. A nice couple was there in a 4X4 when it happened, so they gave us a push and that got us home.

title: Waymo robotaxis kept illegally passing school buses after software fix, feds say
raw_summary: Nearly a year ago, Waymo updated its self-driving software and issued a recall after numerous reports that its robotaxis were illegally passing school buses that had stopped and deployed flashing red lights. Now, federal safety regulators have opened a new investigation into why that behavior has continued. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) said in a November 6 filing that a majority of these reported incidents occurred after the company deployed a software update intended to fix the problem.
summary: Nearly a year ago, Waymo updated its self-driving software and issued a recall after numerous reports that its robotaxis were illegally passing school buses that had stopped and deployed flashing red lights. Now, federal safety regulators have opened a new investigation into why that behavior has continued.
article_paragraphs: Nearly a year ago, Waymo updated its self-driving software and issued a recall after numerous reports that its robotaxis were illegally passing school buses that had stopped and deployed flashing red lights. Now, federal safety regulators have opened a new investigation into why that behavior has continued.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) said in a November 6 filing that a majority of these reported incidents occurred after the company deployed a software update intended to fix the problem.

Waymo said last year that a software update was completed for all affected vehicles on November 17, 2025. However, NHTSA said the majority of the incidents occurred after the software update. NHTSA’s Office of Defects Investigation (ODI) has opened a “recall query” to “assess the adequacy of the remedy.”

The ODI opened its initial investigation into Waymo in October 2025 after seeing footage of one of its autonomous vehicles maneuvering around a stopped school bus that had its stop sign extended, lights flashing, and was unloading children in Atlanta. In that incident, a Waymo robotaxi crossed perpendicularly in front of the school bus from its right side. The autonomous vehicle then turned left around the front of the bus before traveling down the street.

Numerous other incidents have been documented in the weeks and months since in Austin, where Waymo also operates a robotaxi service. Austin Independent School District officials reported at least five such incidents at the time, according to a letter filed with NHTSA.

Reached for comment, Waymo stressed the importance of safety to its mission. “We have made significant improvements to vehicle behavior around school buses and have received no citations since March 2026,” a spokesperson told TechCrunch via email. “The Waymo Driver has a clearly demonstrated positive impact on roadway safety. Once received, we’ll work to respond to NHTSA’s query and look forward to continuing our engagement on recall processes for AV software that continues to learn and improve.”
TechCrunch also reached out to Austin Independent School District officials for comment and will update the article if they respond.

article_paragraphs: Was the Brazilian Grand Prix the best race of the 2026 Formula 1 season?
It certainly revealed a lot about the teams and drivers, and their various strengths and weaknesses.
So here's everything we learned at Interlagos, from the subdued way F1's second 2026 title was secured to how F1's latest debutant really got on.
Max Verstappen very strongly hinted that a win was possible in Brazil, even from the back of the grid, had something not gone wrong with his car during the grand prix.

Verstappen didn't know what it was, but he was convinced his car lost aerodynamic performance during the race. He first noticed it when switching from intermediates to slicks, when the car suddenly had extreme high-speed oversteer.

When he went back to intermediates for the last stint as the rain returned at the end of the race, he said it felt like a night-and-day difference to how it had been at the start. That was all the proof Verstappen needed that something wasn't quite right with the car.

Despite this, he charged from 21st on the grid to finish second, only 14.6s behind race winner Norris. Whether he would have beaten Norris outright is obviously a complete hypothetical. But, maybe he would have at least been close enough to have a go.

There is evidence on Isack Hadjar's side of the Red Bull garage that Verstappen could have had a stronger stint, especially on the softs. Hadjar was really quick in this grand prix, especially in certain phases. He spent a decent chunk of the race quicker than Verstappen, even when they were on the same tyre and the same strategy: he was faster on 22 of the 38 laps where they can be compared directly.

I stopped by the LiveWire booth at EICMA 2026, where the company had everything from its new lightweight S4 Honcho models to the freshly acquired DUST electric dirt bikes – plus STACYC’s electric balance bikes for the youngest riders.
It’s quite a spread, and perhaps more importantly, it paints a picture of a company that increasingly wants to have an electric two-wheeler for just about every stage of a rider’s life.
I also had a chance to spend several hours test-riding the S4 Honcho Street in Milan, so be on the lookout for that article and video to experience it with me.
Perhaps the most important bikes at the booth were the S4 Honcho models, LiveWire’s new lightweight and lower-cost electric motorcycles.

The production S4 Honcho Street made its European debut at EICMA alongside the dirt-oriented S4 Honcho Trail. The Trail version recently began reaching customers in the US, with the Street now en route to dealerships, and European sales are beginning around the EICMA launch.

These bikes represent a significant departure from LiveWire’s earlier strategy. Instead of trying to compete directly with full-size gasoline motorcycles on outright performance, the Honcho platform is aimed at riders looking for something smaller, simpler, and more approachable.
Also on display was the new S4 Honcho Skate, making its first public appearance.

The Senate has scheduled a procedural vote to begin consideration of the draft legislation tomorrow.

On Friday, Sierra Club issued a statement that it could not support the permitting bill as currently written, outlining fundamental changes that must be made. The manager’s amendment partially addressed these concerns, but major substantive issues remain.
In response, Sierra Club Executive Director Loren Blackford released the following statement:

“The Sierra Club appreciates the improvements made by the manager’s amendment, but the draft legislation remains deeply flawed. The Senate must allow an open amendment process for additional changes to be made.

“Updating and expediting transmission and clean energy permitting is essential to delivering lower costs, reduced air, water, and climate pollution, protecting communities, and expanding the grid for the American people. But rushing legislation that erodes Tribal sovereignty and people’s right to have a say in what is built in their communities, abandons clean water safeguards, and wildlife protections, while further enabling a rogue president that is waging a war on clean energy and our public lands is not an acceptable outcome.

“Senate Democrats have been given a mandate to act decisively to deliver relief on energy bills and level the playing field for clean energy. They can and must fight for a better deal. Unless additional dialogue and changes can happen, the Sierra Club cannot support this legislation.”

article_paragraphs: The Ram Rampage is a compact unibody truck that is off-limits to U.S. buyers. Three years after the debut of the model in South America , Stellantis decided to give Europeans a taste of the Brazilian-made lifestyle pickup by bringing over two high-spec trims – the rugged Rebel and the sporty R/T. However, the starting price of the EU-spec Rampage makes American full-size trucks feel like bargains.

The compact model is priced from €44,000 ($49,200) before taxes. Naturally, this is higher than Brazilian pricing , which currently ranges between R$199,990-225,490 ($36,300-41,000) depending on the specification. Distribution in major European markets is handled by importer KW Auto, with the first deliveries expected in February 2026.

To put the Ram Rampage price into perspective for American buyers, the much larger Ram 1500 has a starting MSRP of $42,025 for the entry-level Tradesman trim, while the better-equipped Big Horn will set you back $47,280. That means Europeans are paying more for a compact, unibody pickup with a four-cylinder engine than Americans pay for a full-size truck with a six-cylinder mill.

While the Ram Rampage competes with the Ford Maverick and Renault Niagara in South America, it will be the only compact unibody pickup in Europe. This means that the only alternatives will be traditional midsize pickups such as the Ford Ranger and the Toyota Hilux. Speaking of which, the Ford starts at €46,590 ($52,200) in Germany, and the Toyota at €46,746 ($52,300) in the same market.

Still, Ram targets lifestyle buyers, which is why only the flagship trims of the Rampage made it across the Atlantic. In this context, equipment is quite generous with a 12.3-inch infotainment, a 10.3-inch digital instrument cluster, leather upholstery, 12-way power front seats, Harman Kardon audio, and Level 2 ADAS.

The more adventurous Rebel trim gets plastic cladding and rides on 17-inch wheels shod in all-terrain rubber, while the road-focused R/T stands out with a sportier body kit, a lowered suspension, a louder exhaust, and 19-inch alloy wheels.

The Rampage measures 198 inches (5,028 mm) long and rides on the Jeep Compass-sourced Small Wide unibody platform with a multilink rear suspension setup. The bed has a loading capacity of 980 lt (34.6 cubic feet) and a payload between 1,653 and 2,238 lbs (750-1,015 kg), with the maximum figure being comparable to one-tone midsize pickups.

Under the hood, the EU-spec Rampage offers the option between two non-electrified four-cylinder powertrains. The Rebel is fitted with a 2.2-liter turbodiesel producing 197 hp (147 kW / 200 PS), while the R/T is powered by a turbo 2.0-liter gasoline engine producing 268 hp (200 kW / 272 PS). In both cases, power is transmitted to all four wheels via a nine-speed automatic gearbox.

While battery electric vehicles (BEVs) represent just 4.2% of the global fleet, they now account for 25% of all new car sales worldwide – up from 6.6% five years ago. This surge has pushed oil displacement from 215,000 barrels a day in 2021 to 1.2 million barrels a day today, or roughly 1.2% of global consumption.

At the same time, electric buses now make up 5% of the global fleet, battery electric trucks are at 1% but in some countries exceed 50% of new sales. T&E estimates these vehicles avoid as much as 320,000 barrels a day. As road transport burns close to half of all the world’s oil, transitioning to EVs is crucial in reducing oil dependency. As the global car and truck fleet continues to grow, EVs are the only thing stopping runaway oil demand, warns T&E.

As electrification takes center stage at this year’s COP, current policies put battery electric cars on track to displace roughly 5.8 million barrels of oil a day by 2034 — matching the sustained disruption seen during the 2026 crisis. Accelerating EV adoption will be crucial to preventing future oil shocks, according to T&E.

Antony Froggatt, senior director at T&E, said: “Electric vehicles are the single most effective way of cutting oil demand. Right now the only winners in our oil addiction are fossil fuel giants and petrostates. Places with near 100% sales of EVs like Norway, Denmark and Hong Kong have effectively insulated themselves from future shocks. Five years after Glasgow, EVs stand as one of the clearest victories in global climate history. At this year’s COP, world leaders must set binding electrification targets. Not just for the climate, but for national security.”

BEVs on the road now avoid more than 200 Mt of CO 2 -equivalent a year. According to T&E, rapid transport electrification is a vital part of the wider energy transition by providing essential grid flexibility and storage. Just as past COPs accelerated the global boom in wind and solar, backing for electric vehicles at COP31 can deliver the same breakthrough, slashing oil demand and driving emissions down.

[1] Displaced oil is estimated from daily per vehicle savings: about 0.019 barrels per car (derived from Ember ), 0.2 per truck ( IEA ) and 0.15 per bus (bottom-up from typical fuel use and mileage). The 2026 supply loss has been estimated at 5.8 million barrels a day . We use IEA fleet projections for 2030 and 2035 fleet sizes to calculate the offset year of the BEV car fleet. Results exclude plug-in hybrids, vans and two- and three-wheelers.

raw_summary: The GR Yaris isn’t going anywhere, and a road-going version is reportedly on the way. Toyota has officially confirmed that the Celica is making a comeback. We've known about the Japanese brand's plans to revive this iconic nameplate for some time, and it's now finally been revealed that the Celica will compete in next year's World Rally Championship alongside the GR Yaris Rally1 that motorsport fans know.
article_paragraphs: The GR Yaris isn’t going anywhere, and a road-going version is reportedly on the way.

Toyota has officially confirmed that the Celica is making a comeback. We've known about the Japanese brand's plans to revive this iconic nameplate for some time, and it's now finally been revealed that the Celica will compete in next year's World Rally Championship alongside the GR Yaris Rally1 that motorsport fans know.

New regulations in the top Rally1 class of WRC mean car manufacturers are no longer limited to competing in just a single model, so Toyota can run the all-new Celica alongside a new version of the GR Yaris Rally1. Toyota was spotted testing a mysterious two-door rally coupe at the start of this year, prompting speculation that it was a new Celica designed to replace the Yaris. Claims that the car was the Celica have proven to be accurate, although it will race alongside the Yaris, rather than supersede it.

In September, an updated prototype of Toyota's new GR Celica Rally1 car was filmed up close. It looks significantly different from the GR Yaris Rally1 that competed in the 2026 WRC season, with a lower front end and headlights similar to the Corolla sold in Europe. Other key elements of this prototype include a gaping-wide grille, a large hood vent, a roof scoop, boxy front and rear quarter panels, and a large fixed rear wing.

Speaking with DirtFish , Toyota technical director Tom Fowler confirmed that the GR Celica Rally1 and GR Yaris Rally1 are identical under the skin and that it's competing with the Celica largely as a "marketing tool." While the two rally cars share most of their components, they have unique bodywork. Both will use turbocharged 1.6-liter engines, though Toyota hasn't confirmed if it'll use a three-cylinder or a four-cylinder.

The Toyota Celica has a long and rich history in the World Rally Championship. It made its international rally debut in 1972 and later competed in the Group B era of the mid-1980s with the Celica Twin Cam Turbo. After the Group B class was banned, Toyota created the Celica GT-Four and went on to claim drivers' championships with it in 1990 and 1992 with Carlos Sainz Sr., as well as claiming titles with Juha Kankkunen in 1993 and Didier Auriol in 1994. Toyota has also had lots of recent success, winning the past six manufacturers' titles.

If news of the Celica returning to the top form of rallying isn't enough to get you excited, the fact that a road-going Celica is just around the corner should. In addition to developing a new mid-engined platform that could revive the iconic MR2, Toyota is hard at work on a new Celica that you'll be able to walk into a dealership and buy. The last Celica was built in 2006, so its return will be long overdue.

Recent reports point towards the new Celica using the same basic front-engined setup as the superb GR Corolla hot hatch. Unlike that car, the Celica should debut with Toyota's new turbocharged 2.0-liter four-cylinder rather than a turbocharged 1.6-liter three-cylinder. With a larger turbocharger, this engine can make up to 600 horsepower for motorsport use, though road-going versions should settle around 400 hp. Next-generation versions of the GR Yaris and GR Corolla are also tipped to use this engine, as is the MR2. The new street-legal Celica should pair this 2.0-liter mill with an advanced all-wheel-drive system and is expected to be available with a six-speed manual and an eight-speed automatic transmission.

title: Philadelphia Carjacking Crew Targeted New Toyota SUVs For African Export
raw_summary: Car theft is an issue all over the globe. In most cases, though, instances of it are isolated. According to the U.S. Attorney's Office, a crew in Philadelphia was so coordinated that it was stealing specific Toyota models for resale in Africa . Now, five members have received sentences ranging from 35 years to life plus more than a 100 years. Authorities announced the sentences on November 2, following convictions earlier this year. Court records offer a closer look at the Toyota targeting and the phone records that helped investigators identify suspects. Back in late 2025, a court opinion laid out how the operation worked. Masked attackers operated in small groups, targeted newer-model SUVs like the updated Toyota Land Cruiser , carried handguns, and frequently struck or shot victims. Investigators linked some incidents through ballistic evidence and descriptions of the vehicle used by the attackers, though digital records were apparently just as vital.

Attorney's Office, a crew in Philadelphia was so coordinated that it was stealing specific Toyota models for resale in Africa .
