article_paragraphs: Car theft is an issue all over the globe. In most cases, though, instances of it are isolated. According to the U.S. Attorney's Office, a crew in Philadelphia was so coordinated that it was stealing specific Toyota models for resale in Africa . Now, five members have received sentences ranging from 35 years to life plus more than a 100 years. Authorities announced the sentences on November 2, following convictions earlier this year. Court records offer a closer look at the Toyota targeting and the phone records that helped investigators identify suspects.

Back in late 2025, a court opinion laid out how the operation worked. Masked attackers operated in small groups, targeted newer-model SUVs like the updated Toyota Land Cruiser , carried handguns, and frequently struck or shot victims. Investigators linked some incidents through ballistic evidence and descriptions of the vehicle used by the attackers, though digital records were apparently just as vital.

Mikal McCracken, 24, received life plus 138 years. Amin Muse, also 24, received life plus 55 years, while Aleem Abdul-Hakim, 23, received life plus 28 years. Dean Fosque, 28, was sentenced to 86 years, and Kavon Coleman, 24, received 35 years. Their convictions followed an eight-week trial involving more than 100 witnesses. That might sound excessive for car theft, but people died as a result of these crimes.

On February 6, 2022, the crew killed one carjacking victim but forgot the key fob for the vehicle at the scene of the crime. To resolve the issue, they hired a locksmith to make a replacement. Not long after the theft, police tracked down the vehicle and recovered it. Worried that authorities would identify the locksmith through forensic evidence and that he'd cooperate, the crew planned and carried out his murder. That's where the digital link comes in because police began leveraging court-authorized searches of cellular towers .

Those searches allowed them to link two devices present at multiple carjackings. Warrants allowed police to arrest and indict some of the crew. McCracken challenged the searches, with other defendants joining his effort to exclude the evidence. The judge denied that motion, upholding the warrants and finding that the good-faith exception would also prevent suppression. The same phones investigators believed were needed to coordinate the attacks helped them identify the people behind the carjackings.

raw_title: São Paulo Grand Prix Proves F1 Can Still Thrill In The Rain
title: São Paulo Grand Prix Proves F1 Can Still Thrill In The Rain
raw_summary: Rain is often called the great equalizer in Formula 1, with slippery conditions making driver ability far more crucial to success than car performance. F1 rekindled its wet-weather magic on Sunday in São Paulo, Brazil. As the dominant Mercedes team faltered, 2025 champion Lando Norris showed poise through changing conditions to take his third victory this season. The weekend at Interlagos broke the recent trend of rain halting on-track action instead of shaking up the competitive order. Actually racing in the rain had become as rare as spotting a dodo bird in the wild. Saturday previewed both sides of the wet-weather coin. After a heavy downpour delayed Q1 by more than an hour, fans were treated to one of the season's best qualifying sessions. Wily veterans Fernando Alonso and Nico Hülkenberg dragged their subpar equipment into Q3. They were joined in the final segment by Red Bull's often-scrutinized prospects Liam Lawson and Isack Hadjar . In all, nine teams slotted into Q3's 10 spots.

They were joined in the final segment by Red Bull's often-scrutinized prospects Liam Lawson and Isack Hadjar . In all, nine teams slotted into Q3's 10 spots.

An approaching storm cut the fight for pole into a one-lap shootout. Norris put his McLaren on provisional pole, and George Russell hoped to beat the lap time. However, the Mercedes driver was impeded by Williams' Alex Albon and reassured by his team that he could squeeze in a second lap. When heavy showers proved another run was impossible, Russell lashed out over the radio. Team principal Toto Wolff had to chime in to calm him down.

Norris wasn't as fortunate at the start on Sunday. With the track still wet from earlier rain, the field took to the grid on intermediate tires. Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli actually slid off the track on his reconnaissance lap. The new world champion would have much better traction from his second-place grid box. He launched past the McLaren for the lead into Turn 1 with Lawson following him into second. More action unfolded behind the leaders. Despite starting 20th, Lewis Hamilton flew through the field and was ninth by the end of the opening lap. Max Verstappen made it to 11th from 21st.
Watch the seven-time world champ charge through the field at the start 🤩 #F1 #BrazilGP pic.twitter.com/M685ysLctw

F1's phenoms didn't just leverage their wet-weather prowess, but also adapted better to the changing conditions. After prodding the Ferrari pit wall, Hamilton was the first driver to switch to slicks on lap 14 of the 71-lap contest. The seven-time champion, making his 400th career start, was immediately the fastest driver on track. With a dry line forming, the challenge was getting the tire up to the optimum temperature on the cool track. Russell spun in the pit exit after his stop. Others ran wide into the runoff areas in corners.
Here's Antonelli's spin at Turn 1 which handed Norris the lead 👀 #F1 #BrazilGP pic.twitter.com/bZRcgm07h5

The biggest casualty was Antonelli, who lost the lead to Norris on lap 19 after spinning in Turn 1. He had reported a strange issue where his Mercedes was pulling one side under acceleration. The issue would also crop up on Russell's car. The rain would return with 10 laps to go, but Norris safely swapped back to inters and cruised to the finish line. The only thing that went wrong for Norris was him shattering his champagne bottle on the podium.

article_paragraphs: Tesla is launching its Robotaxi service in San Antonio, its eighth city, with a launch geofence covering about 274 square miles. That’s the biggest day-one map Tesla has ever posted, and more than four times the size of Waymo’s San Antonio service area.

But if Tesla’s recent maps are any guide, a big chunk of that area won’t be bookable. In Austin, an independent check found the Robotaxi app only accepted pickups and drop-offs in about 59% of the zone Tesla advertises.

Tesla’s official Robotaxi account made the announcement just after midnight local time: “Robotaxi available in San Antonio starting tomorrow, 5am.” It came with a map of the “launch geofence,” a large polygon that runs from Loop 1604 on the north side down to just south of downtown.

Robotaxi Tracker , which measures operator maps and logs fleet sightings, puts the zone at 274 square miles. That covers about 1.0 million residents (51% of the metro) and 721,000 jobs. San Antonio International Airport sits inside the polygon, but it isn’t served.

Waymo started driverless rides in San Antonio in February with more than 60 square miles and opened to all riders in October, airport trips included. Robotaxi Tracker currently lists Waymo’s San Antonio area at 59 square miles.
What Tesla didn’t say is how many cars will cover its 274 square miles. As of Monday morning, Robotaxi Tracker hadn’t logged a single Tesla Robotaxi in San Antonio.
The launch landed the same day Tesla expanded Austin again. The tracker now measures Tesla’s Austin zone at 443 square miles, up 178 square miles since mid-September.

We’ve seen this movie. Last month, Tesla expanded its Houston geofence into the shape of a rocket , and within two days the creator of Robotaxi Tracker found the app refusing downtown pickups inside it .

title: After 2 Billion Miles, Ford Releases Mach-E Battery Report Card
raw_summary: 95% of 2021 model year Mustang Mach-Es still have a battery life above 87%, including high-mileage cars How concerned should prospective EV buyers be about battery degradation? Based on a recent study that Ford conducted with its 2021 Mustang Mach-E models, it appears that the battery degradation fears of many are overblown.
article_paragraphs: 95% of 2021 model year Mustang Mach-Es still have a battery life above 87%, including high-mileage cars

How concerned should prospective EV buyers be about battery degradation? Based on a recent study that Ford conducted with its 2021 Mustang Mach-E models, it appears that the battery degradation fears of many are overblown. In fact, after analyzing more than 36,000 Mach-Es sold in the U.S. and Canada, Ford has revealed that they retained an average battery state of health of 92%.

The Mustang Mach-E first hit the market during the 2021 model year, and Ford sold more than 36,000 units that year, providing the automaker with plenty of data as to how these EVs perform in the real world. A key factor in that data is the mileage that customers have collectively racked up on their 2021 Mach-Es, which amounts to more than two billion miles driven — or more than the distance required to travel to Uranus.

Ford says that of the vehicles it has analyzed, 95% of them have batteries sitting at between 87% and 97% health. For the more than 2,000 owners who have driven their Mach-Es in excess of 100,000 miles over the past five years, the average battery health is sitting at approximately 91%. More than 30 drivers have driven their EVs over 200,000 miles, and the battery health of these vehicles averages an impressive 88%. Two owners of 2021 Mach-Es have covered more than 300,000 miles, and one of them is David Blenke , who has driven his Mach-E more than 400,000 miles on the original battery. Ford hasn't specified the battery health of his EV, simply stating it has "remained strong."

"This is one of the most valuable feedback loops we have had at this scale: more than 36,000 vehicles, five-plus years and billions of real-world miles," Technical Leader of High-Voltage Battery Cells and Systems at Ford, Kevin Vander Laan said. "Over five years, billions of miles and verified owner data give us a meaningful, real-world view of battery state-of-health over time. The data is encouraging, and the learnings continue to inform how Ford approaches battery systems, software guidance, and future electric vehicle programs."

The Mustang Mach-E was Ford's first series EV of the modern age, designed to give the company a much-needed rival to the Tesla Model 3 and Tesla Model Y. It uses the brand's Global Electrified 1 architecture, and 2021-2022 models were sold with standard- and long-range battery packs. Evidently, these batteries can handle high mileage with minimal degradation and should certainly last the lifetime of the vehicle without needing a replacement.

Ford's next important EV is the Fathom pickup truck . This new model will start at $29,945 and be the first to use the company's Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform. Its shell will be made using large aluminum castings , it will feature bidirectional charging , and use a simplified 400-volt electric architecture with the company's fifth-generation battery management system.

title: Ford Drops Hint About New Fathom EV Battery Life
raw_summary: The Ford Motor Company has been playing its forthcoming Fathom electric pickup truck close to the vest, releasing few details ahead of volume production except for the MSRP of $28,350. Still, some clues have dropped. The latest news involves a newly released real-life data analysis of five-year battery capacity for the Ford Mustang Mach-E. The findings raise expectations for the next generation of Ford EVs, namely, the Fathom, which is the first vehicle to roll down the tree-like assembly line of the company’s new “Universal EV” platform . On one level, the comparison between the Mach-E and the Fathom EV battery is apples-to-oranges. The 2021 Mach-E deployed [correction: NCM (nickel-cobalt-manganese) batteries with Standard Range at 68 kWh usable capacity as launched, and Extended Range at 88 kWh usable capacity as launched]. Ford is equipping the Fathom with an LFP (lithium-iron-phosphate) EV battery. LFP is a relatively new, more economical formula than Li-ion. All else being equal the tradeoff is lower range, though some Ford watchers point out that drivers can order their Fathom with an optional extended-range battery.
summary: The Ford Motor Company has been playing its forthcoming Fathom electric pickup truck close to the vest, releasing few details ahead of volume production except for the MSRP of $28,350. Still, some clues have dropped. The latest news involves a newly released real-life data analysis of five-year battery capacity for the Ford Mustang Mach-E.
article_paragraphs: The Ford Motor Company has been playing its forthcoming Fathom electric pickup truck close to the vest, releasing few details ahead of volume production except for the MSRP of $28,350. Still, some clues have dropped. The latest news involves a newly released real-life data analysis of five-year battery capacity for the Ford Mustang Mach-E. The findings raise expectations for the next generation of Ford EVs, namely, the Fathom, which is the first vehicle to roll down the tree-like assembly line of the company’s new “Universal EV” platform .

On one level, the comparison between the Mach-E and the Fathom EV battery is apples-to-oranges. The 2021 Mach-E deployed [correction: NCM (nickel-cobalt-manganese) batteries with Standard Range at 68 kWh usable capacity as launched, and Extended Range at 88 kWh usable capacity as launched]. Ford is equipping the Fathom with an LFP (lithium-iron-phosphate) EV battery. LFP is a relatively new, more economical formula than Li-ion. All else being equal the tradeoff is lower range, though some Ford watchers point out that drivers can order their Fathom with an optional extended-range battery.

The point is that the 2021 Mach-E is old news. The new news is the forthcoming Fathom, which Ford has been regularly teasing as the first product of its secret, not-so-secret “skunkworks” team for the past five years or so. The addition of a cost-cutting, internal inverter for bidirectional charging is the topic of the most recent news drop, indicating that Ford expects Fathom drivers to use their EV battery for stationary applications as well as drive time.

Drivers who routinely use the bidirectional feature will likely put their Fathom through more charging cycles than a typical EV, and prospective buyers will need some assurance that their zero emission pickup will be up to the task.

And, that’s where the 2021 Mach-E data comes in. Ford has just released the 5-year numbers for retained battery capacity over time, and they look pretty good. By releasing the data now, when the Fathom is nearing volume production, Ford has raised expectations that the new electric pickup truck will deliver similar, if not better, longevity.

Correction: The Mach-E data doesn’t just look pretty good, it looks very good. Ford deployed its telematics platform to assess more than 36,000 Mustang Mach E’s in the “class of 2021,” driven in the US and Canada over an average ownership period of 5.2 years as of August 2026, during which time drivers clocked a collective 2 billion miles.
The 2021 Mach-E was sold with both standard and extended range battery packs, and the data combines both variations.

Relative to the Fathom’s bidirectional charging feature, the key finding is that high-mileage vehicles scored well. “More than 2,000 owners have crossed 100,000 miles on their original battery pack while maintaining >91% average health,” Ford explains. In the 2021 cohort, 30 drivers also ran past 200,000 miles while retaining an average capacity of about 88%.

He was quote-tweeting a Tesla fan telling people to “get it while you can.” So yes, this is also a sales pitch.

On Friday, Musk announced Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas around mid-2027 “to make room for increased Cybercab production.” That was the first story. Now it’s about “complexity” and “opportunity cost.” Let’s go through it.

Tesla built the Cybertruck supply chain for 250,000 units a year, and its latest shareholder letter still lists more than 125,000 units of installed capacity. In Q3 2026, it delivered 8,295 “Other Models.” With Model S and Model X out of production, we estimated 7,000 to 8,000 of those were Cybertrucks . That’s a 30,000-a-year pace, down 48% year-over-year in that category.
If orders had been outrunning production at any point this year, Tesla had about 95,000 units of idle annual capacity sitting right there. It didn’t use it.

raw_summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk is defending the Cybertruck and the company’s decision to stop producing the polarizing steel-clad truck, claiming that the order rate far exceeds its production. summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk is defending the Cybertruck and the company’s decision to stop producing the polarizing steel-clad truck, claiming that the order rate far exceeds its production. Tesla will shut down production of the Cybertruck in about eight months Musk said in an X post on Monday.
article_paragraphs: Tesla CEO Elon Musk is defending the Cybertruck and the company’s decision to stop producing the polarizing steel-clad truck, claiming that the order rate far exceeds its production.

Tesla will shut down production of the Cybertruck in about eight months Musk said in an X post on Monday. He also said the company will try to make as many of the vehicles as possible before then, though Tesla will “have to return deposits for a lot of people.”

Musk argued the Cybertruck was not unprofitable, and that Tesla was ending production because the “opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck is vastly outweighed by the value of incremental Cybercab production.”

In other words, Musk is arguing that Tesla can make more money by using the factory space and resources dedicated to the Cybertruck for building Cybercab robotaxis. Musk said last week that Tesla plans to use the factory space to build more two-seater Cybercabs.

The first Cybertrucks were delivered to customers in late 2023, when it seemed like it could be a breakthrough hit for the company. Reservations for the vehicle had ballooned to 1 million, according to Musk , who also predicted that the company would sell around 250,000 of the trucks annually.

But those reservations never translated into actual sales. Tesla doesn’t break out sales of the Cybertrucks, but industry experts estimate a total of about 71,000 Cybertrucks have been sold since the first deliveries began in November 2023.

Many of those sales came from inside Musk’s ecosystem of other businesses. For instance, SpaceX (now known as SpaceXSI), which he also leads and is the largest shareholder of, purchased $131 million worth of Cybertrucks from Tesla in 2025, according to the company’s S-1 registration statement ahead of its IPO. Another Musk company, xAI, also bought $430 million worth of Tesla Megapacks for its data centers, before it merged with SpaceX.

But sales of the Cybertruck, which lagged for months, could see a final bump now that it’s going out of production. Still, even a scarcity boost is unlikely to push the truck’s demand to the lofty projections from several years ago.

article_paragraphs: Sure, SUVs are popular, but that doesn’t mean they’re always the best choice for your needs. Here, we’re looking at the subcompact SUV segment and stacking up these small crossovers against compact cars from the same brand.

Subcompact SUVs are the smallest of their species. As the name suggests, they’re smaller than compact SUVs , and their tidier footprints often mean compromises in space, fuel economy, and driving satisfaction.

Automakers feel the need to offer additional ground clearance and all-wheel drive in these SUV models to justify their categorization. But these models typically share the same underpinnings and engines as their compact-car kin.

This means these SUV models are often heavier, less enjoyable to drive, and less fuel-efficient than their non-SUV siblings. Both types of vehicles also typically offer similar amounts of cargo and passenger space. Pricing, meanwhile, tends to favor the compact hatchbacks.
If these two types of vehicles are so similar, then why the different classifications? Blame size creep.

Cars and SUVs typically get larger with each passing generation. Let’s roll the clock back 25 years. While most modern compact cars are bigger than their counterparts from a quarter century ago, they still tend to cast smaller shadows than mid-size cars from the turn of the millennium.

On the other hand, the subcompact SUVs of today are typically larger than the compact SUVs of 25 years ago. Due to this, calling a modern SUV “subcompact” better describes its size relative to the overall SUV landscape as opposed to the larger passenger-vehicle space.

Odds are that if you’re shopping for one of these small-sized SUVs , you’re going to be just as well—if not better—served by these vehicles’ often less expensive and more fun-to-drive compact hatchback stablemates.

For nearly a decade and a half in the 1980s and '90s, Chrysler's K-Car served as the basis for over three-quarters of the company's automotive output. During that span, the humble FWD platform spawned nearly fifty different models, encompassing family cars, wagons, sports cars, limos, and Chrysler's savior minivans.

We looked at an amazingly clean example of one of those models last Friday: a 1986 Chrysler LeBaron Town & Country with fewer than 4,000 miles. It was a total throwback, and in beautiful shape. Still, nice as it was, few of you wanted to step into that time machine, especially at its $18,900 asking price. Ultimately, the comments dunned the LeBaron as just a crappy K Car, with the voting going likewise in an 82% 'No Dice' loss.

In antiquity, Milan, Italy, then known as Mediolanum , served as the capital of the Western Roman Empire. Today it serves as the locus of both Italy's automotive and fashion industries. With all that history, it's surprising that today's 1977 Cadillac Seville Milan isn't named for the Lombardy capital.

Instead, both the car and the company, Milan Coach Builders, were named for the car's designer and company founder, Milan Daniels. Built in small numbers (reportedly fewer than 500), the Milan was not sanctioned by Cadillac or GM.

Private parties would bring their already-purchased Sevilles to Milan's shop, where the cars were cut in half, shrunk from a 114-inch wheelbase to 96 inches, and fitted with a convertible top. Lost in the process were the roof, rear doors, and the back seat. At the time, the idea was to create an American analog to the Mercedes SL, a model that the Milan's dimensions purposely aped. Optionally, Milan Coach Builders also offered a fiberglass hood with a central bump, and an accompanying Rolls-style Parthenon grille.

The result looks less like a Mercedes SL and more like Internet sensation and beloved role model for overcoming adversity, Seattle's Jimothy the Raccoon. That's not a bad association, and considering that upwards of 500 people sent their then-very-expensive Cadillacs to go under the knife, it's obvious these cars have some appeal.

The conversion was only offered on the first-generation Sevilles, and Milan Coach Builders shuttered in the early 1980s after that model ceased production. This one, in white over a white leather interior and charcoal canvas top, is claimed to be in decent condition.

title: Force Motors To Launch Traveller EVs In Q1 2027
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - The electric Traveller range has completed development and is undergoing final testing and homologation Force Motors is getting closer to bringing its Traveller electric vehicles to market. The company plans to launch its first electric models based on the Traveller platform in the January-March quarter of 2027, with an electric ambulance expected to be part of the initial line-up. The development work is already complete, according to managing director Prasan Firodia. The vehicles are currently undergoing final testing and homologation with the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI). Force Motors had showcased an electric version of the Traveller at the 2024 Auto Expo, but commercial sales have not begun so far. The company intends to introduce multiple electric variants of the platform, which serves a range of applications including ambulances, school buses, employee transportation, police vans and delivery vehicles. This gives Force Motors an opportunity to target several commercial applications rather than limit the electric Traveller to conventional passenger transport. The Traveller will be the first step in Force Motors’ wider electrification plans. An electric version of the Urbania people carrier is also under development, although it is still a few months away from entering the homologation stage. The company plans to electrify its other vehicle platforms in phases. However, Firodia expects the shift to electric mobility in the passenger-carrier segment, particularly for vehicles below seven metres, to be considerably slower than what the market has witnessed in electric two-wheelers and passenger cars. The economics of running an EV, range limitations and the availability of charging infrastructure remain important considerations for fleet operators. School transportation could be among the early adopters, given its predictable routes and daily running distances. Tourism and inter-city operations, on the other hand, involve less predictable travel patterns and can make charging logistics more complicated. Force Electric Ambulance rendering Force Motors is investing Rs 3,000 crore across manufacturing capacity, engineering, electrification, hybrid driveline technology and digitisation. It is also working towards increasing its production capacity to 85,000 vehicles. The Traveller EV programme will be an important test of how electric mobility can work in specialised commercial applications. Ambulances, in particular, have very different operating requirements from regular passenger vehicles, making factors such as range, charging time and vehicle uptime crucial. For now, Force Motors has not disclosed the launch prices or detailed specifications of its upcoming Traveller EV range. Those details are likely to emerge closer to the market introduction.

article_paragraphs: Finally, the United States gets the Patrol, even if it's technically a trim for right now

Nissan has sold the Armada in the U.S. and the Patrol overseas for a decade, and despite the different names, they're essentially the same vehicle. Now, Nissan is bringing these two nameplates together in the U.S. with a special version of the Armada called the Patrol Pro-4X. It replaces the old Pro-4X and is the first model to use the Patrol name in America since 1969.

The new Patrol Pro-4X shares the same off-road philosophy as the outgoing Pro-4X and features the same modifications. For all intents and purposes, the two models are the same, except for the name. Nissan says it's bringing back the Patrol name to the U.S. to celebrate 75 years since the Patrol debuted in 1951. It hinted at the nameplate's return when it unveiled the wild Armada June Patrol Concept at SEMA last week .

For Armada owners planning to take their almighty SUVs off the tarmac, the Patrol Pro-4X will be the logical choice. It comes standard with an electronically locking rear differential, a metal skid plate, and adaptive electronic air suspension. Further bolstering its off-road credentials are special 20-inch wheels with all-terrain tires and the Invisible Hood View camera that essentially allows drivers to see what's under the engine bay on the infotainment screen. This system is perfect for avoiding rocks and boulders.
For the new 2027 Armada Patrol Pro-4X, shoppers can order it with several accessories, including new Nismo rock sliders, a Nismo roof rack, and distinctive Nismo Axis wheels with BFGoodrich rubber.

The introduction of the Patrol-branded model coincides with the launch of the full 2027 Armada family. Last year's entry-level Armada SV 4x2 has been axed, and now positioned at the base of the family is the SL 4x2, priced from $66,565, including destination and handling. This is up slightly from the $65,805 MSRP of the 2026 model. The Armada SL 4x4 sticks around for 2027 and is priced from $69,565.

The range then steps up to the Platinum 4x4 priced from $78,065, or a hefty $2,300 increase over last year's model. Nissan has ditched the Platinum 4x2 and Platinum Reserve 4x2 models from 2026, further simplifying the range. Prices for the Patrol Pro-4X are the real headline, with it starting at $81,265. That's a significant $4,690 premium over the outgoing Pro-4X. Completing the 2027 Armada range are the $82,965 Nismo 4x4 and the Platinum Reserve 4x4, priced from $86,865.

All Armada versions use the same twin-turbocharged 3.5-liter V6. In the SL, Platinum, Platinum Reserve, and Patrol Pro-4X models, this V6 delivers 425 horsepower and 516 pound-feet of torque. Fitting of its name, the Nismo 4x4 is upgraded to 460 hp . A nine-speed automatic transmission is shared across the range. Production of the new Patrol Pro-4X will start this month.

raw_title: Electric dirt bikes keep getting called e-bikes. The bicycle industry wants that to stop
title: Electric dirt bikes keep getting called e-bikes. The bicycle industry wants that to stop
raw_summary: The line between electric bicycles and electric motorcycles has been getting increasingly blurry – though perhaps not because the vehicles themselves are actually that hard to tell apart. Instead, much of the confusion comes down to terminology. High-powered electric dirt bikes capable of reaching motorcycle-like speeds are increasingly being referred to as “e-bikes,” despite sharing relatively little with the low-speed electric bicycles millions of Americans use for commuting and recreation.

Instead, much of the confusion comes down to terminology. High-powered electric dirt bikes capable of reaching motorcycle-like speeds are increasingly being referred to as “e-bikes,” despite sharing relatively little with the low-speed electric bicycles millions of Americans use for commuting and recreation.
article_paragraphs: The line between electric bicycles and electric motorcycles has been getting increasingly blurry – though perhaps not because the vehicles themselves are actually that hard to tell apart.

Instead, much of the confusion comes down to terminology. High-powered electric dirt bikes capable of reaching motorcycle-like speeds are increasingly being referred to as “e-bikes,” despite sharing relatively little with the low-speed electric bicycles millions of Americans use for commuting and recreation.
Now the U.S. bicycle industry is asking federal regulators to make that distinction much clearer.

PeopleForBikes , the bicycle industry’s leading trade association, recently testified before the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC), calling for stronger federal regulations that specifically distinguish electric bicycles from higher-powered e-motos and electric dirt bikes.

“E-bikes and e-motos are fundamentally different products, and federal safety regulations need to reflect that distinction,” explained PeopleForBikes Policy and General Counsel Matt Moore. “When high-powered electric dirt bikes are marketed as e-bikes, it creates confusion for consumers and puts the credibility of legitimate e-bikes at risk.”

There’s a real nomenclature problem hiding underneath all of this. The term “e-bike” is widely used as shorthand for “electric bicycle,” but it isn’t exclusively used that way. Motorcycles have been called “bikes” for generations, and motorcycle media and riders will sometimes casually refer to electric motorcycles as “e-bikes” too, just in the way a biker refers to his Harley as his “bike”. In fact, it all comes from the same root. We don’t call motorcyclists “motorists”, do we? No… we call them “bikers”.

All of that makes phrases like “legal e-bike” and “legitimate e-bike” that were even used by PeopleForBikes in its arguments somewhat problematic when discussing proposed regulation. The term “e-bike” simply doesn’t mean anything specific, at least not legally.

What actually matters from a legal standpoint is whether a vehicle meets the codified definition of an electric bicycle, not whether someone calls it an e-bike – especially when the term e-bike is practically applied so broadly. In other words, perhaps part of separating electric bicycles from e-motos is being more precise with the terminology ourselves: “electric bicycle” has a specific regulatory meaning, while “e-bike” has increasingly become a much fuzzier colloquial term. As much as some would want the term “e-bike” to mean something with pedals, it simply doesn’t – at least not in North America.

In contrast, Medium Commercial Vehicle (MCV) sales increased by 21.16% to 9,042 units, while Heavy Commercial Vehicle (HCV) sales registered a robust 28.95% growth. The ‘Others’ category also nearly doubled its volumes, recording 71 units, up 97.22% from 36 units in October 2025.

The segment also maintained strong momentum on a year-to-date (YTD) basis. CV retail sales during April–October 2026 stood at 7,02,405 units, marking an 18.17% increase over the 5,94,384 units recorded during the corresponding period last year.

Diesel-powered vehicles continued to dominate the commercial vehicle market, accounting for an overwhelming 81.40% share of total retail sales in October 2026. CNG/LPG vehicles followed with an 11.31% share, while petrol/ethanol models accounted for 2.97%. Electric vehicles (EVs) held a 4.29% share, whereas hybrids contributed a marginal 0.03%.

CV retail sales recorded growth in urban markets, increasing 6.51% YoY and 15.47% MoM. Rural markets, meanwhile, registered a 6.51% MoM improvement but witnessed a 2.29% decline on a YoY basis, indicating relatively subdued demand in these regions.

Commercial vehicle retail sales list saw Tata Motors leading with 39,914 units sold in the past month to command a 34.67% market share. At no. 2, Mahindra sales declined to 31,500 units, down from 38,602 unit sales of Oct 2025. The company reported a dip in market share to 27.36%.

Ashok Leyland sales improved to 20,774 units from 17,797 units on a YoY basis taking up market share to 18.04%. VECV secured fourth position with 9,603 units sold last month, a volume growth of 1,668 units over 7,935 units sold in Oct 2025. Market share also improved to 8.34% from 7.05% YoY.

CV retail sales of Maruti Suzuki declined to 5,041 units in the past month from 6,147 units sold in the same month last year. This also brought down market share to 4.38% from 5.46%. Force Motor sales went up to 2,363 units in Oct 2026 while Daimler recorded retail sales at 2,205 units.

Mercedes’ eActros 600 packs a whopping, 621 kWh battery that helps the trucks cover 500 km per charge, allowing fleets to move goods between ports and regional fulfillment centers, charging along the way , or while they’re getting loaded and unloaded at their destination, all the while saving the fleet serious money – even before the latest Iran War sent diesel prices skyrocketing .

That big battery sends electrons to Mercedes-Benz’s proprietary electric drive axles, which deliver 1.61 kWh / mile efficiency while rolling out at an average of 36 metric tons (~79,400 lbs.) combined vehicle weight – specs that rivals the theoretical efficiency claims of the Tesla Semi . Except in the real world. And in winter .

The company recently expanded its eActros lineup to include over 40 possible configurations, giving customers a choice of two cab designs, two or three battery packs, multiple wheelbases and new axle configurations, covering everything from short-haul drayage to serious, off highway vocational work.

article_paragraphs: This is a 2006 Yamaha YZF-R6 that’s remained untouched and unused in its factory crate since it was delivered new to the dealer over 20 years ago.

Yamaha’s R6 is one of the most beloved (and begrudgingly respected by its competitors) middleweight superbikes of its time, and the 2006 model came with a slew of major upgrades – including an all-new, more powerful engine with an advertised redline of 17,500 rpm.

Yamaha took its last orders for the R6 on August the 31st, 2026, these final machines are track-only race bikes, built to order for Japanese buyers, and deliveries begin on February the 26th, 2027. That will officially end a model line that began with the 1999 road bike , a 600 with a 15,500 rpm redline whose engineers were told to beat every other 600 on sale.
This is a 2006 Yamaha YZF-R6 that’s remained untouched and unused in its factory crate since it was delivered new to the dealer over 20 years ago.

The R6 was the second step in what Yamaha called its “European Motorcycle Strategy,” after the YZF-R1 of 1998. Perhaps unsurprisingly, both bikes had the same project leader, Kunihiko Miwa. The Yamaha R1 team spent time riding in Europe in March of 1995 to work out what their bike should be, and the R6 team made the same trip the following summer, with the same intentions.

Yoshihiko Takeuchi, a member of the development team, said in an interview published in early-1999 that he would have preferred the bike to replace the YZF600R Thundercat, because he didn’t want it seen as a “lesser” R1. The team’s answer was to treat the R1 itself as their target. Yasunobu Kano, who laid out the frame, said he tried as far as possible not to look at the then-current R1 or talk to its engineering team.

Yamaha’s formal brief asked for the best performance of any 600 superbike in the world at the time, a motorcycle that wouldn’t be left behind when ridden alongside an R1, and the strongest possible base for Supersport racing. Miwa added a number of his own – 200 PS per liter (197 bhp). He wanted to make an impact on the market, and by the time the bike was arriving at dealers, it was clear that he’d succeeded.

The engine was a new 600cc (actually 599cc) inline-four with double overhead cams, four valves per cylinder and an over-square 65.5 mm bore and 44.5 mm stroke. The cylinders were cast in one piece with the upper crankcase and plated rather than sleeved.

title: How the Racing Bulls pendulum is swinging back towards Lawson
raw_summary: When job security is in short supply, there's one solution for an Formula 1 driver. Be so good they can't ignore you. That's easier said than done, but it certainly seems to be what Liam Lawson has taken to heart as he battled for his future over the recent Americas triple-header. summary: When job security is in short supply, there's one solution for an Formula 1 driver. Be so good they can't ignore you. That's easier said than done, but it certainly seems to be what Liam Lawson has taken to heart as he battled for his future over the recent Americas triple-header.
article_paragraphs: When job security is in short supply, there's one solution for an Formula 1 driver. Be so good they can't ignore you.

That's easier said than done, but it certainly seems to be what Liam Lawson has taken to heart as he battled for his future over the recent Americas triple-header. Having been an integral part of Racing Bulls' rise to fifth in the constructors' championship, which will be the Anglo-Italian team's best-ever result, Lawson took ninth in Austin before bagging a pair of seventh-place finishes in Mexico and Brazil.

Following his challenger Nikola Tsolov's strong FP1 debut in Mexico, and Lawson's unfortunate run-in with Red Bull's stalwart Max Verstappen , signs are now pointing towards the pendulum having swung back in Lawson's favour with a decision expected over the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend next week. A report from The Race, which Autosport understands is accurate, says Lawson is now set to stay put after all with Tsolov coming on board as a reserve in 2027. Sources have indicated a final decision is close but not signed off yet.

Driving for his future has been exhausting for Lawson, even if it's not a new situation for the 24-year-old. Ever since he arrived as a deputy for the injured Daniel Ricciardo in 2023, Lawson has effectively been fighting for his seat, first from the sidelines and then as Ricciardo's full-time replacement with little to no job security beyond the next race weekend. It all came to a head over the past triple-header as Racing Bulls and the wider Red Bull organisation kept delaying a final call between Lawson and Tsolov. If Racing Bulls had been a standalone team, the decision to retain Lawson and Arvid Lindblad would have been a no-brainer. Rookie Lindblad is still seen as potential Red Bull material in the future. And while that window appears to have come and gone for Lawson, he has amassed 89 points as the highest point scorer outside the top four teams. With Racing Bulls tasked to train young drivers for the Red Bull senior team though, it is understood Red Bull's Austrian parent company is particularly excited by F2 frontrunner Tsolov's promise. However, a decision to keep Lawson wouldn't necessarily work against Racing Bull's objective, as having such a solid benchmark in the other car has been useful to gauge Lindblad's performances this year too. Meanwhile, 19-year-old Tsolov would still benefit from a full year as a reserve driver, which includes more FP1s, private testing and simulator work.

Racing Bulls has also been explicitly asked by Austria to stand on its own feet both in terms of identity and performance, so that's why a dyed-in-the-wool F1 veteran like team principal Alan Permane would have been keen to maximise performance and stick with Lawson. "The main factors are, as always, pace and speed. That's the very first thing we look for," Permane said when grilled on the topic on Friday in Sao Paulo. "But we're not just a team that exists solely to compete. We are here to bring young talent through, so we have to keep an eye on that. And that doesn't necessarily mean that we just keep churning young talent through the car. We need to maybe have some experience as well to measure that talent."

The clearest hint that a difference in opinion between the various stakeholders is what has really been holding up the decision came from Lawson himself. "I feel like Alan's been extremely supportive to me and I appreciate that a lot," he said. "I've enjoyed working closely with him and with the team this year. Obviously, it's a big organisation so..." Permane recently inked a fresh deal until 2031 as Racing Bulls team principal and co-CEO, so it's obvious that his opinion carries plenty of weight. And it would stand to reason that Permane has wanted some assurances about his share in the decision-making before committing.

"Alan is doing a tremendous job, and the progress the team has made is a direct reflection of his experience, commitment and competitive mindset," said Permane's boss Oliver Mintzlaff, CEO Corporate Projects and Investments Red Bull. "He brings clarity, composure, and a deep understanding of what it takes to perform in Formula 1, while creating an environment where people can consistently deliver at their best."

Meanwhile, fans of Lawson and the team have been flooding the squad's social media channels urging it to re-sign the Kiwi. He said: "I appreciate all the support. I've seen it over the last few weeks. It's honestly really nice to see.

Be so good they can't ignore you.

title: Tesla expands robotaxi service to San Antonio
raw_summary: Tesla is expanding its robotaxi service to another Texas city as it seeks to compete with Waymo and position itself as more than just an automaker. The company said in a post on X that it will make its robotaxis available in San Antonio starting at 5 a.m. local time on Monday. Tesla didn’t provide any additional details about the service, such as the hours of operation, whether the fleet will offer customers its gold, two-seater Cybercab as well as its modified Model Y vehicles, or if these vehicles will have human safety monitors on board. But if the company follows its playbook of previous launches, it will start with a limited number of vehicles and a confined service area, and expand slowly from there.
summary: Tesla is expanding its robotaxi service to another Texas city as it seeks to compete with Waymo and position itself as more than just an automaker. The company said in a post on X that it will make its robotaxis available in San Antonio starting at 5 a.m.
article_paragraphs: Tesla is expanding its robotaxi service to another Texas city as it seeks to compete with Waymo and position itself as more than just an automaker. The company said in a post on X that it will make its robotaxis available in San Antonio starting at 5 a.m. local time on Monday.

Tesla didn’t provide any additional details about the service, such as the hours of operation, whether the fleet will offer customers its gold, two-seater Cybercab as well as its modified Model Y vehicles, or if these vehicles will have human safety monitors on board. But if the company follows its playbook of previous launches, it will start with a limited number of vehicles and a confined service area, and expand slowly from there.

Tesla CEO Elon Musk for a decade promised his company would deliver autonomous vehicles, and it eventually launched a robotaxi service in Austin in June 2025. The launch, though limited and supported by human safety operators on board, was an important milestone for the company and a test of whether self-driving cars could be safely deployed using just cameras and end-to-end AI.

Since then, Tesla has slowly expanded. In January, the company removed safety monitors from its robotaxis in Austin, officially kicking off a true driverless service, and has spent the last 11 months expanding within the city, and to new cities in Florida and Texas. It now operates robotaxis in limited areas of Miami and Orlando as well as Dallas , Fort Worth, and Houston.

Its rival Waymo also operates a robotaxi service using a mix of driverless Jaguar I-Pace and Zeekr RT vehicles, branded Ojai, in Austin, Dallas, Houston, and San Antonio. The company, a subsidiary of Alphabet, recently restarted services in San Antonio after a five-month pause following incidents in which its vehicles got stuck after entering flooded roadways.

While Tesla has more than 400 autonomous vehicles registered in its Austin fleet, its fleets in other cities have numbered between a handful and a few dozen, according to Texas vehicle registration data and the Robotaxi Tracker website . For example, Tesla has just 24 vehicles in Fort Worth and five in Miami, according to the tracker.

Tesla also has a ride-hailing service, under a transportation charter permit, that it operates in the San Francisco Bay Area. While the vehicles are often described as robotaxis, they are operated by a human behind the wheel. Tesla currently doesn’t have the required permits to operate a driverless ride-hailing service in California.

In spite of this expansion push, the company released data this summer that showed its robotaxi network drove fewer miles with paying customers in the second quarter than it did in the first, TechCrunch reported in July.

title: The 'fear' Martin banished with his injured Qatar GP ride
raw_summary: Jorge Martin says his injury-limited ride in the Qatar Grand Prix helped him overcome a specific "fear" at the circuit - even if it didn't do much for his MotoGP title hopes in 2026. Martin had to pull out of the Malaysian Grand Prix after breaking his wrist in the Phillip Island sprint, but gutted it out through the full Qatar weekend two weeks on from the fracture.
summary: Jorge Martin says his injury-limited ride in the Qatar Grand Prix helped him overcome a specific "fear" at the circuit - even if it didn't do much for his MotoGP title hopes in 2026. Martin had to pull out of the Malaysian Grand Prix after breaking his wrist in the Phillip Island sprint, but gutted it out through the full Qatar weekend two weeks on from the fracture.
article_paragraphs: Jorge Martin says his injury-limited ride in the Qatar Grand Prix helped him overcome a specific "fear" at the circuit - even if it didn't do much for his MotoGP title hopes in 2026.
Martin had to pull out of the Malaysian Grand Prix after breaking his wrist in the Phillip Island sprint, but gutted it out through the full Qatar weekend two weeks on from the fracture.

He was too strength-deprived to manage a good qualifying, but picked up third in the sprint, before settling for a quieter seventh place in the main race to leave Qatar 60 points down on Marc Marquez - with 74 left available.

Martin, however, was particularly pleased to see out the weekend incident-free, especially as in the main race he found himself low on energy and with Fabio Di Giannantonio behind - a repeat of the circumstances from April of last year, when Martin fell and was struck by Di Giannantonio's Ducati, suffering rib fractures and a collapsed lung.
"I think I 'unblocked' one more fear," Martin told The Race of his grand prix ride this Sunday. "Every time I went into that corner 12, with Diggia behind, it was honestly a s**t feeling.
"It wasn't nice. But I was fully concentrated, with much more knowledge about myself, about the bike, about the control I have, so I was able to go through that corner in a good way."
Martin's current deficit means Marquez would already win the title with a win in the Portimao sprint, so the efforts to prolong the title battle are likely to have been for naught.
"Very tired. For sure the effort was worth it but now I feel a lot of pain," added Martin. "Luckily, I have two weeks to recover, so I hope that in Portimao I will be at my almost 100%.

raw_title: Which Generation Of Hyundai Tucson Is Safest According To The IIHS
title: Which Generation Of Hyundai Tucson Is Safest According To The IIHS
raw_summary: Car safety has come a long way since the days of yore. Ask the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS). The organization's crash testing standards have evolved significantly over 30+ years as more new vehicles keep getting better at protecting their occupants. By now, we're pretty familiar with the IIHS Top Safety Pick awards. However, just because your second-gen 2011 Hyundai Tucson has the Top Safety Pick under its belt doesn't mean it's as safe as the third-gen 2021 model, which also happens to be a Top Safety Pick winner. Although the IIHS rates the small SUV highly , understand that it also keeps updating the award's eligibility criteria as the years go by. For example, headlights were not even part of the Top Safety Pick criteria in 2010, nor were vehicle-to-vehicle or pedestrian crash-prevention features. And Top Safety Pick+ wasn't even a thing before 2013. In fact, looking at the many generations of the small SUV, it's fair to conclude that fourth-generation Tucsons (2022-2026) appear to be the safest, according to the IIHS. Not only have certain fourth-generation Tucsons gone through the organization's slew of updated testing standards, but they have consistently been part of the IIHS Top Safety Pick+ category between 2022 and 2026, unlike the third or prior generation models.

article_paragraphs: Car safety has come a long way since the days of yore. Ask the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS). The organization's crash testing standards have evolved significantly over 30+ years as more new vehicles keep getting better at protecting their occupants. By now, we're pretty familiar with the IIHS Top Safety Pick awards. However, just because your second-gen 2011 Hyundai Tucson has the Top Safety Pick under its belt doesn't mean it's as safe as the third-gen 2021 model, which also happens to be a Top Safety Pick winner.

Although the IIHS rates the small SUV highly , understand that it also keeps updating the award's eligibility criteria as the years go by. For example, headlights were not even part of the Top Safety Pick criteria in 2010, nor were vehicle-to-vehicle or pedestrian crash-prevention features. And Top Safety Pick+ wasn't even a thing before 2013. In fact, looking at the many generations of the small SUV, it's fair to conclude that fourth-generation Tucsons (2022-2026) appear to be the safest, according to the IIHS. Not only have certain fourth-generation Tucsons gone through the organization's slew of updated testing standards, but they have consistently been part of the IIHS Top Safety Pick+ category between 2022 and 2026, unlike the third or prior generation models.

If you're looking for the safest model year within the fourth generation, the 2026 Tucson looks like the strongest candidate. While models built after March 2024 have fared really well in the updated tests, the eligibility criteria for Top Safety Pick+ have changed between 2024 and 2026, with the most recent update pushing automakers to improve their crash avoidance systems and protection for back seat passengers. Still, despite the tougher rules, the 2026 Tucson meets all the requirements for Top Safety Pick+.

Although the 2026 Tucson won the Top Safety Pick+ award, it's worth noting that the small SUV performed poorly in the IIHS's latest whiplash prevention test . This replaces the original head restraint test that was discontinued in 2022. The new test evaluates three important aspects: "head and spine support, the interaction of the head with the head restraint, and how well the seat handles the energy transfer during impact."

If it means anything, only four out of the first 18 small SUVs tested scored really well and earned a Good rating, according to the IIHS . Although the Tucson isn't part of the group, that's not to say no Hyundai is — the Ioniq 5 was among the SUVs that scored a Good rating, as are the Subaru Forester, Toyota RAV4, and Audi Q3. Joining the Tucson with a poor whiplash prevention score are the Ford Bronco Sport and Mazda CX-50.

According to the IIHS, the Tucson's head restraint pushed the dummy's chin down toward the chest. While most of the vehicles tested were 2025 models, the IIHS says these ratings can apply to certain 2026 models as well. Something similar happened with the aforementioned second-generation Tucson as well. Although all model years except 2014 and 2015 were awarded the Top Safety Pick, they performed poorly in the driver's side small overlap test. IIHS noted that the side curtain airbags didn't deploy, the seatbelts allowed excessive movement, and the dummy's head barely contacted the front airbag. Third-gen and later Tucsons, however, performed considerably better in the test.
Notably, the fourth-gen Tucson received Good ratings in every other area except its LATCH ease of use and headlights (for trims other than Limited), where it received Acceptable ratings.

Webber and his wife Ann – who ran Mark’s career herself back in the day – became Piastri’s managers in 2019, the year the youngster narrowly beat Victor Martins to the Formula Renault Eurocup title and a spot on Renault’s F1 academy.
article_paragraphs: Oscar Piastri and Mark Webber have mutually agreed to terminate their management agreement, the pair have announced.

Webber and his wife Ann – who ran Mark’s career herself back in the day – became Piastri’s managers in 2019, the year the youngster narrowly beat Victor Martins to the Formula Renault Eurocup title and a spot on Renault’s F1 academy.

Piastri’s rise was meteoric from then on, as he clinched the Formula 3 title the following year – again marginally, with Theo Pourchaire and Logan Sargeant just a few points adrift – and won Formula 2 in 2021, also as a rookie, and with little competition that time.

Under Webber, Piastri made the career-defining move to leave the Alpine fold and sign a McLaren race deal for the 2023 Formula 1 season, which paved the way for his 2025 title bid. Across 88 career starts so far, the Australian has taken six pole positions and nine victories.
“We are proud to have played a pivotal role in the formative years of Oscar's career and to have placed him in F1 so that he could compete at the front so early on,” Webber said.

“Following our reduced trackside involvement this season, we have collectively agreed that now is an appropriate time to bring our management agreement to a close. This will allow Oscar to build on his achievements under a new management structure, and for us to embark on our new ventures. We wish Oscar all the very best for a long and successful career.”

Piastri added: “I'd like to thank Mark and Ann for all their support and advice over the years. Their guidance has been invaluable, particularly in navigating the beginning of my F1 career. I wish them all the best going forward.”

Webber had taken a step back at the start of the 2026 season and no longer supported Piastri trackside, with a couple of new figures assisting the McLaren driver – Pedro Matos, his race engineer at Prema in Formula 2, and mental coach Emma Murray.

article_paragraphs: The flagship luxury sedan from BYD comes with high-tech features and high-quality materials

Chinese automakers may have developed technology that makes Western rivals jealous , but they still lag behind in terms of originality. The perfect example is the flagship model of BYD's high-end sub-brand Yangwang, dubbed Altior. The luxury sedan comes loaded with features such as tank-turn and flotation capabilities, but it looks like a Rolls-Royce Phantom with a Yangwang face.

The production model debuted during the weekend in Abu Dhabi, targeting sedans from well-established automakers such as Rolls-Royce, Bentley, and Mercedes-Maybach. The Yangwang Altior measures 5,600 mm (220.5 in) long, which makes it 55 mm (2.2 in) longer than a Rolls-Royce Ghost and 162 mm (6.4 in) shorter than a standard-wheelbase Phantom.

The styling language of the Goodwood brand clearly served as the source of inspiration for BYD designers. From the side, the EV looks like a Rolls-Royce replica, with the signature proportions, greenhouse, chrome inserts, suicide doors, and character line that stretches from the nose to the tail. The bi-tone treatment and the design of the polished 21-inch wheels are also quite familiar.

Naturally, the Altior needed a few unique styling features in order to avoid any legal troubles with BMW Group, although BYD claims it took inspiration from an ancient Chinese ceremonial vessel called ding. At the front, the complex headlights with twelve rotating and sequentially illuminating elements have a similar shape to those of the Yangwang U8 SUV , although in the sedan they are connected to the lower bumper intake.

The boxy grille trades the Spirit of Ecstasy for the gold oracle-bone-script emblem of Yangwang and features a special pattern with jewel-style elements. The rear end is much simpler, with horizontally-arranged taillights sending subtle Lincoln Continental vibes , chrome accents and a minimalist rear bumper.

The front and rear suicide doors open by 80 degrees and 90 degrees respectively, revealing a luxurious four-seater cabin. Yangwang used high-quality materials for the cabin, such as natural wood inserts, semi-aniline leather upholstery, silk embroidery, wool floor mats, and real metal for the switches.

Party tricks include a screen-covered dashboard, a powered 21.4-inch overhead display for the rear passengers, a 39-speaker audio system with rising and rotating tweeters, a pair of zero-gravity massaging and reclining rear seats, front and rear refrigerators, and door-mounted umbrella holders just so Rolls-Royce owners feel at home.

raw_title: BYD Yangwang Altior Comes To The Fore As A Flagship Luxury Statement
title: BYD Yangwang Altior Comes To The Fore As A Flagship Luxury Statement
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - BYD Yangwang Altior electric sedan features four individual motors and an executive rear cabin alongside a claimed CLTC range of over 1,000 km BYD previously introduced the Yangwang U8 SUV and U9 hypercar to showcase its advanced vehicle technology. The Altior now takes the luxury brand into the executive sedan category after its global unveiling in Abu Dhabi a couple of days ago. The four-seat electric flagship features a long wheelbase and an elaborate rear cabin, and it also uses four independently controlled motors and promises more than 1,000 km of driving range under the Chinese CLTC cycle. The rear compartment has two individual reclining seats that feature extending leg rests and mechanical massage systems. Each massage unit uses four ball-shaped heads. The Altior offers 1,209 mm of rear legroom and 354 mm of knee room while a button folds the front passenger seat forward to open the view from the rear executive position. The front doors open to 80 degrees and the rear coach doors to 90 degrees. In addition, an automatic relaxation function adjusts the seats, blinds, lighting and cabin fragrance. The sedan measures 5,600 mm long, 2,030 mm wide, 1,590 mm tall and its wheelbase stands at 3,500 mm. The tall grille features individually polished decorative pieces around the Yangwang emblem and is accompanied by twelve lighting elements illuminate in sequence as the owner approaches. The side profile has a short front overhang and two distinct body creases extending for 4.8 metres. Customers can choose between three wheel designs measuring 21 inches and all three use 275/45 tyres. The e4 electrical architecture assigns one motor to each wheel and adjusts torque distribution more than 100 times every second. The car can also perform a tank turn and has an emergency flotation function for an accidental water incident. Its DiSus active suspension controls body movement in six degrees of freedom. The system assesses the road ahead so the suspension can respond to surface changes. More importantly, the second generation Blade Battery supports the claimed CLTC range and BYD has also confirmed Flash Charging technology. The interior materials are just as distinctive as the exterior proportions. Yellow Hetian jade is used for the air vents and Suzhou embroidery decorates the upholstery. The seats feature full grain semi-aniline leather while pure wool carpeting and natural wood trim are other highlights. BYD says the ornamental elements take inspiration from the ding – an ancient Chinese ceremonial vessel. The controls have real metal surfaces and there are 48 decorative pieces distributed among 11 locations. Rear passengers also get a powered 21.4-inch overhead entertainment display and a 39-speaker Dynaudio Platinum Evidence sound system. The audio system has tweeters that rise and rotate when the vehicle starts. Refrigerators are installed at the front and rear, and the 5.5 litre rear unit can cool or warm its contents. As for practicality, the luggage compartment holds 532 litres. Driver assistance comes from the God’s Eye A system which supports navigation assistance on highways and city roads as well as automated parking functions. The Altior will be offered in Executive and Bespoke editions. Its first themed Bespoke version is called Shanhe Dingyun and uses brown and gold exterior colours and jade inspired interior detailing. The brand said development of the sedan took three years and its Chinese name Dingyao refers to the ceremonial vessel that influenced its styling. The vehicle enables an entirely different type of luxury appeal to Yangwang following the performance based U9 and the U8 SUVs.

A production version of MG GO is planned and it has been spied during TVC shoot for the very first time. Because it was undergoing TVC Shoot, it does not have any camouflage on it and shows all of its production-spec design and detailing ahead of a planned launch.

First showcased at 2026 Goodwood FOS as a concept, the MG GO electric hatchback seems to have entered production and the production-spec version was just spied undergoing TVC shoot. When compared to the concept showcased in July 2026, the production version looks a lot more tamer in comparison.

The rear view cameras on concept make way for sleek rear-view mirrors in White contrast. Production-spec headlights have C-shaped LED DRLs in them and then we can see C-shaped elements in lower bumper as well. There seems to be some sort of closed-off grille in production version and MG badge is in the bumper, like in concept.

Doors have a more pronounced frame and they don’t have frameless windows. Inspired by the concept, we still get flared wheel arches along with those swanky alloy wheels and then those Union Jack like LED signature in the tail lights. Sort of like in a Mini Cooper. Rear spoiler is a large unit and it lends a sporty aesthetic.

On the tailgate, we can see MG GO badging and then a conventional rear windshield wiper and washer. Rear bumpers and side body cladding have Black elements to reduce visual bulk and the overall proportions look like it was inspired by a Mini Cooper. There is a MG badge on rear quarter glass too.

MG GO has been designed by Carl Gotham in London, taking inspirations from legacy MG vehicles like MGB GT, MG Metro Turbo, MG ZR and MG EX4. Immediate rivals for MG GO include Mini Cooper EV, Nissan Micra EV and the Renault 5, among others. Initially, MG GO is expected to be produced only in China and later a CKD route for assembly operations in SAIC’s Ferrol plant in Spain.

Positioned on the E+ platform, MG GO is expected to share the same 43 kWh battery pack as MG4 and a 150 bhp electric motor, driving the front wheels. It could measure around 4 metres in length and will be positioned below MG4 and could carry a price tag of around EUR 20,000 (approx Rs 21.02 lakh). Launch in India is less likely.

raw_summary: Unfamiliar surroundings can elicit feelings of uneasiness. We’re in Madrid; we’ve just rolled out of bed and arrived at Circuito de Madrid Jarama. A few minutes pass, and we’re belted into the passenger seat of the Audi’s newest halo car, the Audi Nuvolari , itself a relatively unexplored place. Site laps are sometimes easy, but not today. article_paragraphs: Unfamiliar surroundings can elicit feelings of uneasiness. We’re in Madrid; we’ve just rolled out of bed and arrived at Circuito de Madrid Jarama. A few minutes pass, and we’re belted into the passenger seat of the Audi’s newest halo car, the Audi Nuvolari , itself a relatively unexplored place. Site laps are sometimes easy, but not today. Our tour guide, Victor, has a crazy look in his eye. And maybe a screw loose. He attacks the braking zones, exits corners sideways, and shows zero restraint in his speed. Victor, we love you, but can you save a little tire for the rest of us?

We enjoyed our first experience with Audi’s first mid-engine car since the dearly departed R8. After just three laps driving around the former home of the Spanish Grand Prix, we love the Nuvolari. Having spent time with the Nuvolari’s donor plug-in hybrid platform, the Lamborghini Temerario , eases the tension.

The Audi’s cabin, a cocoon of microfiber and leather with aluminum door handles, seat controls, and vents, oozes fancy-dinner vibes more so than qualifying laps. It’s a welcoming environment. Strapped into the driver’s seat, the Nuvolari starts up in its pure electric mode. Turning the top-left knob on the busy steering wheel wakes the 789-hp twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V-8; its flat-plane crankshaft is capable of spinning to a bonkers 10,000 rpm. The cabin fills with glorious noise, most of it real. Turning and holding that same knob activates Dynamic+ mode, summons more noise, and puts most of the systems in their most-ready state.
See all results for new 2028 Audi Nuvolari for sale near 20147

Exiting Jarama’s final corner and pointing down the straight, the Nuvolari accelerates as if it were shot off an aircraft carrier’s flight deck. As in the Temerario, the screaming V-8 has friends. A 147-hp motor connected to the crankshaft fills the lulls in the engine’s torque delivery. The front axle has two 147-hp motors that also provide torque vectoring. While the Temerario stores its energy in a 4-kWh battery, the Nuvolari (like the new Lamborghini Revuelto SV ) utilizes a larger 7-kWh pack. The new pack supplies up to 254 horses, compared to the Temerario’s 187-hp limit. In all, the V-8 and electric motors work together to create a 987-hp party, or 80 more than the Temerario.

By the end of Jarama’s nearly half-mile front straight, we’ve almost reached an indicated 185 mph. The Nuvolari brakes as effortlessly as it accelerates, courtesy of Brembo CCM-R Plus carbon-ceramic rotors (16.5-inch up front and 16.1-inch at the rear) that bite hard. The pedal doesn’t feel as wooden as the Lambo’s, where more force yields more stopping power. In the Nuvolari, a spring change within the brake actuator feels like it prioritizes pedal travel to modulate the brakes rather than pressure. Nevertheless, the pedal feels great.
See all results for new 2028 Audi Nuvolari for sale near 20147

Bending the Nuvolari into Turn 2 reveals off-center steering feel that isn’t nearly as over-caffeinated as the Lamborghini’s. Here, it feels very Audi. Effort ramps up in a linear fashion but is never too heavy. It’s as direct as it needs to be, and there’s ample indication when the front tires have had enough.

raw_title: Auto Festive Sales 2026: Dhanteras Spurs Deliveries, October Retail Down 24%
title: Auto Festive Sales 2026: Dhanteras Spurs Deliveries, October Retail Down 24%
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - Maruti Suzuki reported over four lakh festive car sales as FADA recorded 31.72 lakh October vehicle registrations in India Maruti Suzuki reported more than four lakh car sales between Ganesh Chaturthi and Dhanteras in 2026 against 3.46 lakh units in the comparable festive period last year. However, the auto industry recorded a 23.80 per cent annual decline in October retail registrations. The contrasting figures are partly explained by the festival calendar. Diwali fell in October last year but moved to November 8 in 2026 and Dhanteras was also celebrated on November 6. The festive delivery period is mainly important for PV dealerships as manufacturers had dispatched substantial inventory ahead of the celebrations. The Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA) reported passenger vehicle stocks equivalent to 43 to 45 days of sales at the end of October. The figure was unchanged from September and exceeded the association’s recommended level of 21 days. Retail purchases in November will determine how much of that inventory dealers can sell before December. The auto industry registered 31,72,466 vehicles last month. The total was 25.05 per cent above September despite the annual decline as two wheeler registrations stood at 23,21,419 units and passenger vehicles recorded 5,07,768 units. However, both categories reported lower sales than in October 2025. In contrast, commercial vehicles, three wheelers and tractors recorded annual increases and achieved their highest October registrations. Vehicle Category Oct 2026 Sales YoY October Record Two wheelers 23,21,419 -28.35% Second highest Passenger vehicles 5,07,768 -14.23% Third highest Commercial vehicles 1,15,140 +2.29% Highest Three wheelers 1,41,420 +3.97% Highest Tractors 79,285 +3.10% Highest Wheeled construction equipment 7,434 +22.07% – Total 31,72,466 -23.80% Second highest Electric vehicles recorded a considerably different performance from the overall industry. Nearly 3.55 lakh electric vehicles were registered in October 2026 and the annual increase stood at 44.88 per cent. Its penetration rose to around 11.5 per cent compared to nearly 6 per cent a year earlier. Zero-emission models also constituted close to 63 per cent of three wheeler registrations. In PVs, the combined share of CNG, hybrid and electric models stood at 41.83 per cent against 41.60 per cent for petrol and ethanol vehicles. The Dhanteras celebrations also prompted substantial delivery plans from carmakers. Maruti Suzuki targeted close to 30,000 car handovers on November 6 and Hyundai expected around 16,000 deliveries with over 12,000 from Tata Motors. The estimates indicated substantial festive sales activity but were separate from the final registration figures compiled by FADA. It is worth noting that Maruti Suzuki had delivered around 50,000 vehicles over the two days of Dhanteras in 2025. The two wheeler market faced a more difficult annual comparison. Rural registrations declined by 33.97 per cent against a 20.77 per cent reduction in towns and cities as the later festival dates affected October purchases. But FADA also identified weak agricultural conditions in certain regions and higher vehicle financing costs as big concerns. The association reported that around 31 per cent of dealers faced a moderate or substantial effect from increased financing expenses and loan repayments. FADA also projects that annual automobile registrations could approach 3.2 crore units in 2026 against 2.82 crore in 2025 as PV retail could surpass 50 lakh units for the first time. The complete registration figures this month will establish the final impact of the Dhanteras and Diwali purchases on the festive sales performance.

title: BYD Atto 2 Spied In Chennai
raw_summary: BYD is expanding its portfolio in India with the more premium, more luxurious and the more performant Denza brand . However, the company is also working to expand its entry-level portfolio with the Atto 2. Test mules have been spied in the country before and the latest spy shots are from automotive enthusiast Sarath S, spotted in Chennai. The spied BYD Atto 2 test mule looks like it could be the EV version and was not donning any camouflage at all. This could be a hint that launch could be nearing and this is what BYD Atto 2 could look like when launched in the country.
summary: BYD is expanding its portfolio in India with the more premium, more luxurious and the more performant Denza brand . article_paragraphs: BYD is expanding its portfolio in India with the more premium, more luxurious and the more performant Denza brand . However, the company is also working to expand its entry-level portfolio with the Atto 2. Test mules have been spied in the country before and the latest spy shots are from automotive enthusiast Sarath S, spotted in Chennai.

The spied BYD Atto 2 test mule looks like it could be the EV version and was not donning any camouflage at all. This could be a hint that launch could be nearing and this is what BYD Atto 2 could look like when launched in the country.

From previous spy shots, it is evident that BYD is testing Atto 2 EV in the country. We say this because previous spy shots showed that there was no fuel filler cap on rear left quarter panel where petrol is usually filled in the PHEV DM-i version of Atto 2. The pre electric version of Atto 2 does not have this cap, which was the case with BYD Atto 2 test mule spied testing here.

However, the possibility of BYD launching the Atto 2 DM-i PHEV cannot be thrown into the winds. BYD started its journey in India with e6 and then incorporated Atto 3, Seal, eMAX7 and Sealion 7. Now, BYD is carving out its most affordable model for India, positioned below the Atto 3 to rival electric C Segment SUVs like Hyundai Creta Electric, Tata Curvv EV and Sierra EV.

Launch is expected to happen in 2027 and Atto 2 is expected to boost BYD’s sales and market presence to a new horizon. Atto 2 is also called Yuan Up in China and Yuan Pro in South American nations. Dimensionally, BYD Atto 2 measures 4,310 mm in length, 1,830 mm in width, 1,675 mm in height and has a 2,620 mm long wheelbase.

Atto 2 comes with a boot space of around 400L, expanded to 1,340L. On the outside, notable design highlights include rugged body claddings, sleek LED DRL signature and LED headlights, large alloy wheels, flap-style door handles, interesting C Pillar area, striking rear roof spoiler and connected rear LED tail light signature, among others.

Inside, BYD Atto 2 packs a premium cabin with a 15.6-inch rotatable infotainment screen, an 8.8-inch instrument cluster, ambient lighting, panoramic sunroof, ventilated seats, leatherette upholstery, front and side airbags, advanced Level-2 ADAS and more.

BYD Atto 2 EV is powered by up to 64.8 kWh battery pack sending juice to a single electric motor driving front wheels only. This motor is rated at up to 201 bhp and 310 Nm and the claimed range is up to 430 km (WLTP). BYD promises a 0-100 km/h sprint in 7.9 seconds and DC fast charging.

article_paragraphs: After taking a look at the electric car sales for last month , let us now take a look at the electric two wheelers. India’s electric two-wheeler segment recorded its strongest monthly performance in October 2026, with total registrations reaching 2,24,064 units.

This represented a robust 48.49% year-on-year (YoY) growth compared to 1,50,890 units registered in October 2025. Month-on-month (MoM) sales also increased by 8.08% from 2,07,314 units in September 2026 . In volume terms, the segment added 73,174 units on a YoY basis and 16,750 units over the previous month.

TVS Motor retained its leadership position in India’s electric two-wheeler market, recording sales of 60,490 units in October 2026. This was an impressive 94.66% increase over the 31,075 units sold in October 2025. MoM sales also grew by 11.94% compared to 54,037 units in September 2026.

Bajaj Auto secured the second position with 49,156 units sold, accounting for a 21.9% market share. Sales increased by 51.33% YoY from 32,462 units in October 2025, while MoM growth remained relatively modest at 1.44% compared to 48,429 units in September 2026. Together, TVS Motor and Bajaj Auto registered combined sales of 1,09,616 units, accounting for approximately 48.9% of total electric two-wheeler registrations.

Ather Energy recorded sales of 31,833 units, registering a 5.25% YoY increase and a 4.26% MoM improvement. The company had sold 30,246 units in October 2025 and 30,533 units in September 2026. Hero MotoCorp also reported strong growth, with electric two-wheeler sales rising to 29,923 units in October 2026. This translated into an 81.36% YoY increase and a 23.03% MoM improvement.

Ola Electric, meanwhile, continued to face challenges, with sales declining to 12,098 units. This was a 26.41% YoY decline compared to 16,439 units in October 2025. MoM sales also dropped by 10.06% from 13,451 units in September 2026.

Greaves Electric two wheeler sales went up to 10,839 units in Oct 2026. It related to a strong 39.98% YoY growth from 7,743 units while MoM sales rose by 16.35% as against 9,316 units. River Mobility too has reported improved sales in the past month with triple digit YoY growth. Sales stood at 6,817 units which was a 273.94% YoY development. There had been 1,823 units sold in the same month of last year. MoM sales went up by 22.70% from 5,556 units.

BGauss too recorded improved sales to 5,556 units last month. This was an 80.57% YoY and 10.61% MoM growth. Other electric two-wheeler manufacturers collectively contributed 17,382 units to total registrations. This category recorded 50.81% YoY growth and a 4.41% increase compared to Sept 2026.
